The human implementation provided descriptive comparisons, not same-data validation. Dose proxies, unpopulated co variates, residual imbalance, implementation deviations, and ignored cross-cohort covariance limited interpretation. This case demonstrates a connected workflow whose protocols, code, and results can be reviewed.

items.title_en: Serum proteins predict incident inflammatory bowel disease 14 years before diagnosis: a machine-learning and Cox modelling in the UK Biobank
items.title_zh: 血清蛋白可在诊断前14年预测新发炎症性肠病：英国生物样本库（UK Biobank）中的机器学习和 Cox 建模
items.abstract_en: Using an analysis pipeline that combines machine learning-based feature selection with classical statistical modelling, we aimed to predict incident inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and to identify candidate proteins associated with disease development. We used UK Biobank data in an observational cohort study of 52,331 participants with proteomics data and without a history of IBD. The cohort was split into an 80/20 train/test dataset, and three separate extreme gradient boosting models were trained on the training dataset. Using Shapley values, we ranked the predictive importance of 2,912 proteins for incident IBD, Crohn's disease (CD), and ulcerative colitis (UC). The top 20 proteins per outcome served as features in multivariate Cox models predicting 350 incident cases over 14 years. All three proteomics Cox models showed moderate discrimination in the test dataset, with the UC model performing the best (C-index: 0.68), followed by IBD (C-index: 0.65), and CD (C-index: 0.60). All proteomics models outperformed clinical models. Smoking remained the only significant clinical predictor in the combined proteomics + clinical model. 48 unique proteins were identified across the three models, with 16 reaching statistical significance (p< 0.05). Machine learning-based feature selection with statistical survival modelling identifies plasma proteins that predict incident IBD and highlight biologically plausible, potentially targetable pathways in the preclinical phase of IBD.

items.title_en: Childhood Stress and Amygdala-Hippocampal Volume: A Multiverse Analysis in Adolescents
items.abstract_en: Childhood adversity is robustly linked to differences in amygdala and hippocampal volume. However, findings across studies have been inconsistent and contradictory. This inconsistency stems partly from the many reasonable but arbitrary choices that researchers make when operationalizing brain regions, stress exposure, and covariates. To deal with this variability, we applied a multiverse analysis approach using adolescent data from the Boston Adolescent Neuroimaging of Depression and Anxiety (BANDA) study to evaluate how multiple analytic choices influence the relationships between stress and hippocampal/amygdala volume. Our primary analysis crossed three region-of-interest operationalizations (left, right, total), four intracranial volume scaling methods, and multiple sociodemographic covariates. Greater lifetime stress severity was associated with smaller amygdala volume across 72% of specifications, and with smaller hippocampal volume across 52% of specification models. Statistical significance was strongly influenced by the region of interest. Our secondary multiverse analysis tested six operationalizations of stress exposure (total/acute/chronic x count/severity). This analysis found that the laterality pattern in the primary analysis was not strongly influenced by stress operationalization. These findings demonstrate the robustness of the stress-medial temporal lobe association and identify specific analytic choices (i.e. hemisphere operationalization) that most strongly drive the variability observed in previous literature. Our study is one of the first that utilized multiverse analysis for adversity-neuroimaging research, and provides a strong framework for evaluating and interpreting inconsistent findings.

items.title_en: A Growing Burden, a Persistent Gap: Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome Education and Emergency Department Trends in Michigans Legal Cannabis Market
items.abstract_en: Background: Since Michigan's legalization of recreational adult-use cannabis in December 2018, health care providers in the city of Kalamazoo, Michigan, have informally observed an increase in cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (CHS) presentations, although the extent of this increase has not been formally characterized locally. CHS is frequently underrecognized and misdiagnosed, often resulting in repeated emergency department (ED) visits and substantial diagnostic costs before a diagnosis is reached. Despite this clinical and financial burden, it is unclear whether consumers are adequately informed of this risk through point-of-sale or public health resources. Methods: A cross-sectional environmental scan was conducted to identify publicly available educational content about CHS on the websites of licensed cannabis retailers in Kalamazoo and relevant public health agencies. Provisioning centers and public health websites were screened using a structured coding rubric developed specifically for the environmental scan to assess the presence, depth, web page placement, and intended audience of CHS-related content. Additionally, the electronic medical records at a local teaching hospital in Kalamazoo were queried to identify ED visits with a primary diagnosis of CHS from January 1, 2010 to December 31, 2025. Results: Before the legalization of marijuana, the hospital recorded six ED encounters with the primary diagnosis of CHS between January 2010 and November 2018, and 274 ED encounters between December 2018 and December 2025 (mean age: 29 years; 157 females, 123 males). The incidence rate of CHS-related ED encounters was 57.2 times higher during the post-legalization period than during the pre-legalization period (95% CI, 26.0-157.3; exact Poisson rate-ratio test, p < 0.0001). Among the licensed Kalamazoo provisioning centers reviewed, only one mentioned CHS as a warning but did not describe symptoms or offer medical guidance. CHS content was not identified on the websites of the state or local health departments. Conclusion: Despite the growing clinical concern regarding CHS, consumer-facing educational resources remain scarce. Although this study cannot establish a causal relationship between the availability of CHS-related educational content and the observed increase in ED encounters following legalization, it identifies a substantial lack of CHS-specific warnings in the evaluated consumer-facing resources. Given the clinical and potential economic burden associated with delayed CHS recognition, we recommend that Michigans existing point-of-sale pamphlet requirement be amended to include CHS-specific warning language.

items.title_en: Social patterning of elevated blood lead among children aged 12-59 months in Bangladesh: a national cross-sectional analysis of MICS7 2025
items.abstract_en: BackgroundChildhood lead exposure is a major global health concern. The 2025 Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS7) measured blood lead in a nationally representative sample of children aged 12-59 months for the first time. Preliminary reports suggested elevated blood lead was more common in wealthier urban households, contrary to the usual assumption. MethodsWe analysed 10,622 children with a valid blood lead result (10,458 with complete covariate data for regression models). Elevated blood lead was defined as [≥] 5 {micro}g/dL. Prevalences are survey-weighted with design-based confidence intervals. Associations were estimated with survey-weighted logistic regression using stratified-cluster (Taylor-linearised) variance, and checked with a stratified bootstrap of primary sampling units and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate control. Sensitivity analyses varied the outcome definition, the sample, and the weighting. ResultsSurvey-weighted prevalence of elevated blood lead was 38.5% (95% confidence interval [CI] 37.2-39.9%). Prevalence rose monotonically from 30.2% in the poorest to 51.9% in the richest wealth quintile. In the fully adjusted model, each wealth quintile was associated with 23% higher odds (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 1.23, 95% CI 1.16-1.30), each level of maternal education with 20% lower odds (AOR 0.80, 95% CI 0.76-0.84), and urban residence with 37% higher odds (AOR 1.37, 95% CI 1.18-1.59). Household crowding was associated with higher odds (AOR 1.16 per person per room, 95% CI 1.10-1.24). The wealth-education interaction had AOR 0.95 (95% CI 0.92-0.98). In an exploratory contrast, weighted prevalence was 76.2% among children in the richest quintile with mothers having at most primary education versus 19.5% among those in the poorest quintile with mothers having higher secondary or tertiary education (prevalence ratio 3.9, 95% CI 2.6-6.0). Adjusted odds relative to Barishal ranged from 0.39 in Rajshahi to 3.29 in Dhaka. ConclusionsIn this cross-sectional survey, elevated blood lead was more prevalent among wealthier and urban households and among children of less educated mothers, with large geographic variation. Lead prevention and source-identification efforts should therefore not be restricted to poor communities; prevalence remained high even in the poorest quintile. Interpretation is limited by substantial missing blood lead results and coding uncertainty.

items.title_en: Increase in Surgical Case Mix Index Across a Multi-Hospital System with Structured Limited Surgeon Chart Review
items.abstract_en: Introduction: Hospitals face increasing financial pressures. Hospital reimbursement is tied to the Case Mix Index (CMI). The CMI is a measure of complexity of care provided by the hospital and the total reimbursement is the CMI multiplied by a base pay factor, multiplied by the total number of discharges from the hospital. The few studies in the literature have involved logistically complex attempts to improve documentation. We sought to determine whether limited, structured chart review by surgeons can improve CMI in a multihospital system. Methods: We performed a prospective, observational study in a four-hospital academic medical system on all surgical patients from 10/2022 to 7/2026. Two clinically busy trauma surgeons performed limited structured chart reviews for select surgical patients. In the limited intervention period (1/2024-9/2024) this focused only on the trauma division. In the full intervention period (10/2024-7/2026) expanded to all surgical patients across the system. The main outcome was surgical case mix index (CMI). Results: A total of 35,695 patients were included (13,811 pre-intervention, 9,337 limited intervention, 12,547 full intervention). CMI increased significantly among surgical patients across the whole system (2.68 (95%CI 2.65-2.71) to 2.87 (95%CI 2.82-2.92) to 2.97 (95%CI 2.93-3.01), ANOVA p <0.001). Overall length of stay was unchanged among surgical patients across the whole system. The estimated increase in revenue per patient attributable to this intervention was $3,912 in surgical patients across the system. Conclusion: Having trauma surgeons review targeted surgical patients for high value documentation capture significantly enhanced the CMI and estimated revenue of surgical services across a multi-hospital integrated health system. Such documentation reviews may represent a practical method to improve hospital documentation and revenue.

items.title_en: Individual Angiotensin Receptor Blockers and Risk of Dementia: A Target Trial Emulation Study
items.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Observational studies suggest that angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are associated with lower dementia risk than angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEIs). Whether dementia risk differs across individual ARBs remains uncertain and was investigated in this study. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study emulated target trials using electronic health record and claims data from 44 US health care organizations in the TriNetX Linked Research Network. ACEI/ARB-naive adults aged 55 to 80 years initiating an ARB or lisinopril were eligible. Separate 1:1 propensity-score matching was performed for each comparison. Individual and pooled ARBs were compared with lisinopril (between-class), and non-losartan ARBs with losartan (within-class). The primary outcome was incident all-cause dementia; secondary outcomes included Alzheimer disease, vascular dementia, cerebral infarction, death, and dementia or death. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs. Sensitivity analyses included lagged and treatment-persistence analyses, control outcomes, and E-values. RESULTS: Of 22,025,599 individuals screened, 2,051,275 were eligible; matched cohorts ranged from 10,113 to 857,773, with median follow-up of 4.7 to 7.2 years. Pooled ARBs were associated with lower dementia risk than lisinopril (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.85 to 0.87), with substantial variation across individual agents (HR range, 0.66 to 0.93). Within-class comparisons showed similar heterogeneity (HR range, 0.68 to 0.94) and reproduced between-class agent ordering by HR estimates. Considerable agent-level variation was also observed across secondary outcomes. Losartan, the most commonly prescribed ARB, had the least favorable dementia associations. Negative-control associations were near null within class, and sensitivity analyses supported robustness. DISCUSSION: Individual ARBs were associated with differing dementia risks, suggesting clinically relevant within-class heterogeneity pending confirmation in randomized trials.

items.title_en: Effect of a culturally adapted birth preparedness and complication readiness training intervention on knowledge among Hehe pregnant women in rural Iringa Tanzania: A controlled pretest-posttest quasi-experimental study
items.abstract_en: Abstract Background: Birth preparedness and complication readiness (BPCR) knowledge is important for recognizing maternal and newborn danger signs and preparing for timely care. However, conventional translation of BPCR educational materials may not adequately address local linguistic and cultural contexts. This study evaluated whether a culturally adapted Swahili BPCR training manual improved knowledge more than a standard translated Swahili BPCR training manual among Hehe pregnant women in rural Iringa, Tanzania. Methods: A controlled pretest-posttest quasi-experimental study was conducted among 176 pregnant women attending antenatal care in Mufindi and Kilolo districts. Eighty-eight women received the Culturally Adapted Swahili BPCR Training Manual and 88 received the Standard Translated Swahili BPCR Training Manual. Both groups received comparable BPCR education with standardized session duration, delivery format, language, and follow-up procedures. BPCR knowledge was assessed using a 64-item questionnaire at baseline and four weeks after the intervention. The primary analysis used Difference-in-Differences regression to compare changes in knowledge between groups. Multiple linear regression was used to assess the association between intervention-group assignment and post-intervention knowledge after adjustment for baseline knowledge and participant characteristics. Results: All 176 participants completed both assessments. Mean knowledge scores increased from 21.01 (SD 7.42) to 38.49 (SD 7.54) in the culturally adapted group and from 22.51 (SD 5.80) to 32.81 (SD 5.55) in the standard translated group. The culturally adapted group demonstrated a 7.18-point greater increase in knowledge than the standard translated group ({beta} = 7.18, 95% CI: 4.40-9.97; p < 0.001). After adjustment for baseline knowledge, age, education, gravidity, marital status, living arrangement, reading ability, and occupation, intervention-group assignment remained significantly associated with higher post-intervention knowledge ({beta} = 5.88, 95% CI: 3.84-7.92; p < 0.001). Conclusion: Culturally adapted BPCR education was associated with greater short-term improvement in knowledge than standard translated education among Hehe pregnant women. Integrating culturally and linguistically appropriate terminology, contextual explanations, and locally meaningful communication into BPCR education may strengthen knowledge outcomes. Multisite studies with stronger allocation procedures and longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title_en: Sex workers experiences of HIV prevention, healthcare access and mental health in the West Rand District, South Africa: a qualitative study
items.abstract_en: Sex workers remain disproportionately affected by HIV and mental health distress because their access to prevention and support services is shaped by stigma, criminalisation, violence, poverty, unequal client power, fear of disclosure and negative healthcare encounters. These pressures are particularly visible in district-level settings where sex workers must balance unstable income, personal safety and healthcare needs. A qualitative research design was used. Participants were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling. Twenty unique participants took part in the study: five participated in individual semi-structured interviews and 15 different participants attended two focus group discussions comprising seven and eight participants, respectively. No individual interview participant attended a focus group discussion. Participants were aged 18 years or older and lived or worked in the West Rand District. The interviews and focus group discussions were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed through reflexive thematic analysis informed by Braun and Clarkes six-phase process, with data organisation supported by NVivo. Six themes were developed: sex work as economic survival rather than simple choice; HIV prevention under conditions of unequal client power; healthcare access shaped by stigma, fear and lack of confidentiality; mental health distress as part of everyday sex work; peer educators as trusted bridges to care; and the need for inclusive and differentiated support. HIV prevention and mental health support were interconnected through poverty, client negotiation, clinic mistrust, emotional distress and reliance on peer-led services. Economic insecurity, client power, stigma, weak confidentiality and psychological distress constrained access to HIV prevention and mental health support services. Peer educators facilitated access through information, referrals, emotional support and clinic navigation. Services should therefore be integrated, confidential, stigma-free and responsive to diverse gender identities, sexual orientations and sex-work settings.

items.title_en: An Imaging Risk Score for Bipolar Disorder: Multimodal Comparison and Integration with Polygenic Risk
items.title_zh: 双相障碍的影像风险评分：多模态比较及其与多基因风险的整合
items.abstract_en: Background: Biological risk scores provide objective markers of bipolar disorder (BD) liability. Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have led to polygenic risk scores (PRSs) that capture genetic liability to BD at the individual level. We lack a comparable large-scale effort to leverage a brain-wide association study (BWAS) to create an imaging risk score (IRS) that captures brain structural liability to BD at the individual-level. Here, we conduct the largest multivariate BWAS of BD and develop a BD IRS. We compare the BD IRS to the PRS and assess their combined predictive performance in multimodal risk score (MRS) models. Methods: Our multivariate BD BWAS used 153 structural neuroimaging features from 3902 cases and 6855 controls (mean age (sd)=35.47 years (13.42), 56.70% female) in a cross-validated machine learning approach. Using the resulting model coefficients, we constructed an IRS. We then evaluated the out-of-sample performance of the IRS, PRS derived from the largest GWAS to date, and combined MRS model using logistic regression in a subset of individuals with imaging and genetic data (nBD=486, ncontrols=1701, age (sd)=33.10 (12.02), 56.47% female). We also performed stratified analyses for demographic and BD clinical groups. Prediction performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Subsequent analyses examined associations between each risk score and BD relevant symptoms in developing youth. Outcomes: In predicting case status, the BD BWAS model achieved a mean AUCBD of 0.62 (sdBD=0.08) and in stratified analyses, had higher prediction than subgroup-specific BWAS models. The BD type II BWAS was the only exception (AUCBDII=0.60, sdBDII=0.07 vs AUCBD=0.58, sdBD=0.09). The BD PRS had an AUCBD of 0.65 (CI95%=0.63-0.68) and a higher AUC than subtype-specific PRS in stratified analyses. The PRS typically attained a higher AUC than the IRS. Notably, the IRS and PRS were uncorrelated (r=0.03, p=0.11). MRS models outperformed the prediction of individual PRS and IRS with the strongest prediction for BD type I (AUCBD=0.74, CI95%=0.70-0.78). The IRS had the strongest associations with BD-related symptoms in developing youth including increased energy (OR=1.21, pfdr=0.03) and distress from psychotic-like experiences (OR=1.23, pfdr=0.04). Interpretation: Our BD IRS is a novel biological indicator of BD risk. The lack of correlation between the IRS and PRS along with improved MRS prediction suggests the two risk scores capture some orthogonal liability to BD. We show that integrating imaging and genetics is useful for biological characterization of BD and should be considered for the development of clinically relevant prediction models.

items.title_en: Mortality Among Patients with Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract_en: Objective To estimate the mortality proportion among patients with severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) and to assess variation in mortality according to geographical region, study characteristics, patient populations, and mortality assessment time points. Design Systematic review and meta-analysis. Data sources PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to January 2026. Eligibility criteria Studies reporting mortality among patients with severe TBI were eligible. Severe TBI was defined as a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of [≤]8, equivalent to GCS <9 or GCS 3-8. Studies involving mixed TBI severity were included only when data for patients with severe TBI could be separately extracted. Data extraction and synthesis Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality. Mortality proportions were pooled using a random-effects model. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q and the I2 statistic. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were undertaken where sufficient data were available. Results Twenty-five studies comprising 12,829 patients with severe TBI were included in the systematic review. Across studies, 5,550 deaths were reported. Mortality proportions ranged from 17.5% to 71.1%. The pooled mortality proportion was 40.6% (95% CI 35.7% to 45.7%), with substantial heterogeneity (I2=96.8%, p<0.001). Mortality varied considerably according to geographical region and timing of outcome assessment, with higher estimates generally observed in African settings and at longer follow-up periods. Conclusion Mortality among patients with severe TBI remains substantial, with approximately two in five patients dying across the included studies. However, the very high heterogeneity indicates that the pooled estimate should not be interpreted as a universal mortality risk. Differences in healthcare resources, patient characteristics, injury severity, management practices, and mortality assessment time points may contribute to the observed variation.

items.title_en: Dietary Intake, Handgrip Strength and Elevated Blood Pressure Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults in Peri-Urban Ghana: A Cross-sectional Study
items.abstract_en: Background: Aging is associated with physiological, biological, socioeconomic and psychological changes that may increase vulnerability to poor dietary intake, reduced muscle strength and elevated blood pressure. In Ghana, evidence on dietary intake in relation to functional and cardiometabolic health among community-dwelling older adults remains limited. This cross-sectional study assessed dietary intake, handgrip strength (HGS) and elevated blood pressure (BP), and examined associations between diet quality indicators and these health outcomes among older adults in five peri-urban communities in the La Nkwantanang-Madina Municipality, Ghana. Methods: Data were collected from 200 community-dwelling adults aged 60 years and above. Dietary intake was assessed using a multiple-pass 24-hour dietary recall, while physical activity, HGS and BP were measured using standardized procedures. Categorical variables were summarized as frequencies and percentages. Non-normally distributed dietary variables were compared between health outcome groups using the Mann-Whitney U test. Adjusted binary logistic regression was used to examine associations between diet quality indicators and HGS or elevated BP. Results: The mean age of participants was 69.8 {+/-} 7.3 years. More than half did not meet the dietary reference intake for protein, fat, fiber, magnesium, potassium and vitamin E, and no participant met the dietary reference intake for calcium. The prevalence of inadequate minimum dietary diversity (MDD) and inadequate mean adequacy ratio (MAR) exceeded 50%. Energy, protein, carbohydrate and selenium intake differed significantly by HGS status (p < 0.05). Mean adequacy ratio differed significantly by HGS status (p = 0.021) and BP status (p = 0.016). In adjusted models, each one-unit increase in MDD was associated with lower odds of elevated BP (AOR = 0.68; 95% CI: 0.46-1.00; p = 0.05), while each one-unit increase in MAR was associated with higher odds of normal HGS (AOR = 8.77; 95% CI: 1.33-64.08; p = 0.034). Conclusions: Dietary inadequacy was common among older adults in this peri-urban Ghanaian setting. Better diet quality indicators were associated with normal HGS and lower odds of elevated BP. These findings support the need for nutrition-focused strategies and further longitudinal or intervention studies to clarify the role of dietary intake in functional and cardiometabolic health among older adults.

items.title_en: Logical CCZ state cultivation
items.title_zh: 逻辑CCZ态的培育
items.abstract_en: Logical CCZ states enable Toffoli gates, a central building block of fault-tolerant quantum arithmetic. We introduce an end-to-end protocol for direct CCZ-state preparation on bivariate tricycle and bicycle (BT/BB) codes. Our factory combines the cup-product CCZ gates native to BT codes with two novel ingredients, both enabled by engineering the logical coupling between BT and BB codes through projection-preserving lifts. Index-2 lifted BB ancillas enable selective $Z$-basis initialization, allowing the native cup-product gates to directly prepare two disjoint logical CCZ states. The prepared CCZ states are faithfully transferred to index-3 lifted BB memories with high code distance. We use decoder-based postselection to obtain high-fidelity output states with low overhead. We perform exact simulations of our factory under a circuit-level noise model motivated by neutral-atom hardware, obtaining joint infidelities of $1.84\times10^{-5}$ at $21.94\%$ acceptance and $4.10\times10^{-7}$ at $8.89\%$ acceptance for single-qubit, CZ, and CCZ error rates of $0.01\%$, $0.1\%$, and $0.5\%$, respectively. At the output-infidelity target of our smallest factory, its estimated spacetime cost per CCZ state is lower than that of $T$-state cultivation followed by CCZ conversion, providing an efficient route to logical CCZ states for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
items.abstract_zh: 逻辑CCZ态可实现Toffoli门，而Toffoli门是容错量子算术的核心构件。我们提出一套在双变量三轮车与自行车（BT/BB）码上直接制备CCZ态的端到端协议。该“工厂”把BT码固有的杯积（cup-product）CCZ门与两项新要素结合，二者都借助保持投影的提升（lift）来工程化BT与BB码之间的逻辑耦合。指数2提升的BB辅助态实现选择性Z基初始化，使固有杯积门可直接制备两个不相交的逻辑CCZ态。所制备的CCZ态被忠实转移到高码距的指数3提升BB存储器。我们采用基于解码器的后选择，以低开销获得高保真输出态。在受中性原子硬件启发的电路级噪声模型下对工厂进行精确模拟：当单比特、CZ与CCZ错误率分别为0.01%、0.1%与0.5%时，21.94%接受率下联合不保真度为1.84×10⁻⁵，8.89%接受率下为4.10×10⁻⁷。在我们最小工厂的输出不保真度目标下，其每个CCZ态的估计时空成本低于先培育T态再转换为CCZ的方案，为容错量子计算提供了一条高效获得逻辑CCZ态的途径。
items.highlight_zh: 在BT/BB码上直接培育CCZ态，开销低于T态转换路线
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究了什么问题：容错量子计算机要做算术运算，就需要Toffoli门这类“非Clifford门”，而逻辑CCZ态正是实现Toffoli门的关键资源。传统路线是先用“魔法态培育”造出T态，再把它转换成CCZ态，步骤多、开销大。本文要问：能不能直接在纠错码上“种出”CCZ态，从而更省成本？
2) 用了什么方法：作者提出一套端到端协议，在双变量三轮车码与自行车码（BT/BB码）上直接制备CCZ态。核心是两项新设计，都通过“保持投影的提升（lift）”来调控BT码与BB码之间的逻辑耦合：其一，用指数2提升的BB辅助比特实现选择性的Z基初始化，让BT码自带的杯积（cup-product）CCZ门一次就制备出两个互不相交的逻辑CCZ态；其二，把这些态忠实转移到码距更高的指数3提升BB存储单元中保存。输出阶段用基于解码器的后选择，以较低开销筛出高保真态的样本。作者在模仿中性原子硬件的电路级噪声模型下做了精确模拟。
3) 有什么结果：在单比特、CZ、CCZ错误率分别为0.01%、0.1%、0.5%的设定下，工厂输出的联合不保真度达到1.84×10⁻⁵（对应21.94%的接受率），以及在更严格筛选下4.10×10⁻⁷（8.89%接受率）。
4) 为何重要：即便采用作者最小的工厂配置，按其输出不保真度目标估算，每个CCZ态所需的时空成本也低于“T态培育+CCZ转换”的既有方案。这为容错量子计算提供了一条更高效的逻辑CCZ态来源，也为把BT/BB码这类双变量码用于实际量子算术铺路。

items.title_en: Quantum-Aware Key Rank for Side-Channel Attacks evaluation
items.title_zh: 面向侧信道攻击评估的量子感知密钥秩
items.abstract_en: Side-channel attacks on block ciphers rarely recover the key outright: they leave a residual key space ordered by subkey posteriors, and evaluation laboratories report the key rank of the true key against thresholds near 2^48 and 2^60. No evaluation framework models an adversary who collects traces classically and finishes the search on a quantum computer, although quantum search with advice provides exactly that. We give such an adversary a cost model and a metric. For a device whose key has rank r, any quantum algorithm with classical access to the posteriors needs Omega(sqrt(r)) cipher evaluations, and block search achieves O(sqrt(r)); the per-instance advantage is exactly quadratic, and the super-quadratic exponents reported for search with advice are averages over the prior that apply to no single device. Under the NIST MAXDEPTH budget D and a Grover iteration of g gates and depth d, the quadratic advantage holds only for ranks up to (4D/(pi d))^2 and collapses to a constant factor beyond; with the best published AES-128 oracle and D = 2^40 the window closes near rank 2^58.6. We define the quantum-aware key rank, the classical rank of equal cost, computable from the rank estimators laboratories already run, and derive the classical rank a device must retain to keep a given threshold against each depth budget. Block search and amplitude amplification from the product-form posterior state are within a factor of two to four of each other on Hamming-weight posteriors, so the cost of coherent indexing decides between them. Experiments on simulated leakage and a toy cipher confirm the predicted window: at SNR 0.125 a depth-limited quantum adversary is worth about 22 traces to a classical one, however large its gate budget.
items.abstract_zh: 对分组密码的侧信道攻击很少能直接还原密钥：它们留下一个按子密钥后验排序的残余密钥空间，评估实验室报告真实密钥的密钥秩，并与接近 2^48 和 2^60 的阈值比较。现有评估框架没有刻画这类对手——经典地采集迹、再在量子计算机上完成搜索，而“带建议的量子搜索”恰好对应这一情形。我们为这种对手建立代价模型与度量：对密钥秩为 r 的设备，任何经典访问后验的量子算法都需要 Ω(√r) 次密码评估，而分块搜索可达 O(√r)，单实例优势恰为二次；文献中带建议搜索的超二次指数只是先验上的平均，不适用于任何单个设备。在 NIST MAXDEPTH 预算 D、每步 Grover 迭代 g 门、深度 d 的约束下，二次优势仅在秩不超过 (4D/(πd))^2 时成立，超出后坍缩为常数因子；采用已发表的最佳 AES-128 预言机且 D=2^40 时，该窗口在秩约 2^58.6 处关闭。我们据此定义“量子感知密钥秩”（即等代价的经典秩，可由实验室已有的秩估计器计算），并推导设备为维持给定阈值在每个深度预算下必须保留的经典秩。在 Hamming 权后验上，分块搜索与基于乘积形式后验态的振幅放大相差仅 2–4 倍，因此相干索引的代价决定了二者的取舍。模拟泄漏与玩具密码实验证实了预测窗口：在 SNR 为 0.125 时，受深度限制的量子对手无论门预算多大，约相当于 22 条迹。
items.highlight_zh: 量子二次优势仅在秩≲(4D/πd)²内成立，AES-128窗口止于2^58.6
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究问题：侧信道攻击通常无法直接还原密钥，只能给出按后验概率排序的残余密钥空间，评估机构用“密钥秩”（真实密钥排在第几位）衡量安全性。以往的评估框架只考虑纯经典搜索，没有考虑攻击者“经典采集迹、量子完成搜索”的混合策略。
2) 方法：作者用“带建议的量子搜索”刻画这种对手——经典地拿到后验分布作为建议，再做 Grover 类搜索，并为其建立代价模型和度量。理论上证明：任何能经典访问后验的量子算法至少要 Ω(√r) 次密码评估，而分块搜索可以做到 O(√r)，即单实例优势恰好是二次的；文献里更漂亮的超二次指数只是先验平均的结果，对单个设备不成立。
3) 结果：这个二次优势不是无条件的。在 NIST MAXDEPTH 预算 D 和每步 Grover 迭代 g 门、深度 d 的限制下，只有秩不超过 (4D/(πd))² 时量子才占优，超出后只剩一个常数因子。用目前最好的 AES-128 预言机、D=2^40 时，窗口在秩约 2^58.6 处关闭。作者由此定义“量子感知密钥秩”，并给出设备在每个深度预算下为保住阈值必须保留的经典秩。模拟泄漏和玩具密码实验印证了预测：SNR=0.125 时，受深度限制的量子对手无论门预算多大，只相当于约 22 条迹。
4) 意义：为后量子时代的侧信道评估提供了可操作的阈值修正，说明量子加速是有窗口、有上限的，而非笼统的数量级提升。

items.title_en: Intermediate memory costs of quantum channel synthesis with a protected subsystem
items.title_zh: 带受保护子系统的量子信道合成的中间存储代价
items.abstract_en: A quantum memory can preserve a subsystem perfectly while discarding information needed by a later operation. We study the total intermediate dimension required for channel synthesis when the first stage protects a $b$-dimensional subsystem and has a prescribed noncommutative graph imposing full confusability on an $a$-dimensional control register. For a finite family of classically controlled branches, exact synthesis is possible if and only if the target graph contains the prescribed graph of the first stage. For every feasible family, we construct a single processor that implements all branches exactly. The processor uses pairwise nonorthogonal pure program states in a register of dimension at most $a$. A target graph may be realizable with a carrier of dimension $b$, while synthesizing a channel with that graph can require dimension $ab$. We also characterize the closure of the attainable channels, distinguishing exact synthesis from arbitrarily accurate approximation. Finally, for a family built from the trine communication task, a four-dimensional carrier permits exact synthesis with quantum programs under output depolarization. At the same total carrier dimension and without free shared randomness, classical programs have optimal normalized diamond error $(1-η)/4$, where $0\leqη\leq1$ is the depolarization strength. For $η<1$, the gap persists under sufficiently small perturbations of the target branches.
items.abstract_zh: 量子存储可以在完好保存某一子系统的同时丢弃后续操作所需的信息。我们研究如下情形下信道合成所需的总中间维数：第一阶段保护一个 b 维子系统，并具有一个规定的非交换图，该图在 a 维控制寄存器上强加完全可混淆性。对于有限的一族经典控制分支，精确合成可行当且仅当目标图包含第一阶段的指定图。对每一可行族，我们构造单一处理器精确实现所有分支，其程序态是维数至多 a 的寄存器中两两非正交的纯态。目标图可能仅用 b 维载体即可实现，而合成具有该图的信道却可能需要 ab 维。我们还刻画了可达信道的闭包，区分精确合成与任意精度近似。最后，对于由 trine 通信任务构造的一族，在输出退极化下四维载体即可用量子程序精确合成；在相同总载体维数且无自由共享随机性时，经典程序的最优归一化菱形误差为 (1-η)/4，其中 0≤η≤1 为退极化强度；当 η<1 时，该差距在目标分支的足够小扰动下依然存在。
items.highlight_zh: 保护子系统的信道合成：b维图可能需ab维载体，量子程序优于经典
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究问题：量子存储在合成量子信道时，中间步骤到底需要多大维度的寄存器？本文聚焦一种典型情形：第一阶段要完好保护一个 b 维子系统，同时它的非交换图（用来描述“哪些状态可以相互混淆”）在 a 维控制寄存器上要求完全可混淆——也就是一边保住信息、一边丢弃信息。
2) 方法：考虑有限的一族经典控制分支，先给出精确合成的充要条件：目标图必须包含第一阶段的指定图。对每个可行族，作者构造出一个单一处理器，能精确实现所有分支，其程序态是两两非正交的纯态，寄存器维数不超过 a。随后刻画可达信道的闭包，明确区分“精确合成”和“任意精度近似”。
3) 结果：最关键的发现是一个维度分离——目标图本身可能只用 b 维载体就能实现，但合成具有该图的信道却可能必须用 ab 维。也就是说，图的混淆结构与物理实现资源之间存在乘法级差距。此外，对由 trine 通信任务构造的一族，在输出退极化下一枚四维载体就足以精确合成；在总载体维数相同且没有免费共享随机性的条件下，经典程序的最优归一化菱形误差为 (1-η)/4（η 为退极化强度），且当 η<1 时，这一差距在目标分支的小扰动下仍然保持。
4) 意义：把“保护子系统”这一量子存储能力的真实中间代价量化出来，并给出量子程序相对经典程序的资源优势及其鲁棒性边界，对量子信道的资源理论设计有直接指导意义。

items.title_en: Quantum Work Statistics from Entanglement-Assisted Invariance
items.title_zh: 来自纠缠辅助不变性的量子功统计
items.abstract_en: We demonstrate that the one-time measurement scheme is more consistent than the standard two-time measurement scheme with respect to the fundamental symmetry of entanglement, namely entanglement-assisted invariance (envariance). In particular, the work statistics obtained from the one-time measurement scheme arise naturally as a direct consequence of envariance for any driving unitary, without involving an explicit measurement postulate, whereas the analogous identification for the two-time measurement scheme is possible only for a Haar-measure-zero set of unitaries. This envariance-based formulation eliminates the ambiguity in work statistics related to the energetic cost of measurement.

items.title_en: Effect of deep-trap density of states for a-Si:H layers on HIT cell performances: Modeling Framework
items.title_zh: a-Si:H层深能级陷阱态密度对HIT电池性能的影响：建模框架
items.abstract_en: In this work, an aSi and cSi heterojunction solar cell with an intrinsic layer is simulated using AFORS-HET software. The study focuses on the role of the electronic density of states DOS of the amorphous emitter, p type aSiH, in governing the performance of the HIT cell and the electronic transfer across the heterointerface. It is found that the DOS of the p type aSiH emitter can cause an unfavorable recombination and trapping effect, which becomes more severe and difficult to avoid when the bulk dangling-bond density in the a-Si emitter approaches or exceeds the doping concentration. An increase in deep trap density beyond a critical value causes a drop in the built in voltage and shifts the depletion layer into p type aSi. This situation leads to a sharp decline in HIT cell performance, namely the open circuit voltage and the fill factor, and to the appearance of an S shaped IV characteristic. The simulation results suggest that the emitter activation energy needs to be optimized to achieve high efficiency. Under optimal conditions, holes accumulate near the heterojunction interface, leading to the formation of an inversion layer. This paper presents a physical mechanism for recombination processes within the emitter and concludes with the optimized parameters required to achieve a HIT cell efficiency comparable to Sanyo record of 23 percent on a thin silicon wafer.

items.title_en: Petz Recovery through a Single Polar Transformation for Approximate Quantum Error Correction
items.title_zh: 通过单极变换实现Petz恢复用于近似量子纠错
items.abstract_en: The Petz recovery map provides a near optimal decoder for approximate quantum error correction, but its inverse square-root normalization complicates circuit implementation. We use the polar structure of the Petz recovery isometry to implement recovery through a single quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). We give explicit block-encoding circuits and an extended recovery isometry that yields approximate Petz recovery without postselection. We bound the diamond distance between the approximate and ideal Petz encoding-recovery channels in terms of a spectrum-weighted loss, which provides a channel specific objective for optimizing the QSVT angles. Uniform polynomial approximation yields an asymptotic error bound that decays exponentially with the number of QSVT iterations, at a rate controlled by the smallest nonzero scaled singular value. Applications to Haar-random encoding and the Hayden-Preskill protocol illustrate the tradeoff between circuit depth and recovery accuracy and place existing scrambling decoders within a common Petz recovery framework.

items.title_en: Demonstration of a mobile ion-trap quantum device
items.title_zh: 移动离子阱量子设备的演示
items.abstract_en: Trapped-ion devices are being investigated for transportable applications, including the transfer of exotic charged particles between laboratories and the development of portable quantum technologies. To date, ion transport has been demonstrated only in magnetic (Penning) traps, whereas radiofrequency (Paul) traps are the predominant platform in quantum science. Here, we report the first transport of a few thousand ions confined in a linear Paul trap over distances of several kilometers, with transport durations of 15 and 45 min. These results establish a foundation for mobile trapped-ion quantum devices capable of operating while in motion and may enable the transport of exotic ions in Paul traps between experimental facilities.

items.title_en: Quantum Spectral Estimation with Multiple Initial States: Improved Error and Cost Scaling
items.title_zh: 多初始态的量子谱估计：改进的误差与成本标度
items.abstract_en: We study quantum spectrum and eigenstate property estimation using multiple initial states and generalized Hadamard tests. Building on the QFAMES (quantum filtering and analysis of multiplicities in eigenvalue spectra) framework, we introduce a new method that samples evolution times independently for each initial-state pair. Under the stated assumptions, when statistical error determines the sampling cost, the total Hamiltonian simulation cost required for fixed-accuracy eigenvalue and observable estimation is independent of the number of initial states, up to logarithmic factors. This improves scalability when many initial states are needed to explore the target eigenspaces. The method also reduces the cost of multiplicity recovery and retains Heisenberg-limited scaling for eigenvalue estimation. Numerical experiments support the predicted statistical error scalings.

items.title_en: Universal enhancement of the pairing gap in a dilute Fermi superfluid
items.title_zh: 稀薄费米超流体中配对能隙的普适增强
items.abstract_en: At zero temperature, a dilute Fermi gas with an attractive contact interaction forms a superfluid with gapped fermionic excitations. We show that the gap at weak coupling can be organized as a trans-series expansion in the interaction strength and the asymptotic Gor'kov-Melik-Barkhudarov gap. Low-energy virtual quasiparticles generate corrections that are linear in the gap with a leading coefficient nearly 25$\times$ larger than the other known coefficients. This substantially increases the gap at intermediate densities, highlighting that systematic corrections are crucial for quantitative predictions.

items.title_en: Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
items.title_zh: 退化图行列式与高维杨图
items.abstract_en: Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.

items.title_en: Cavity-tunable Pseudospin-Hall Topology and Edge Transport
items.title_zh: 腔可调谐赝自旋-霍尔拓扑与边缘输运
items.abstract_en: Topological edge states are a hallmark of topological phases, with their existence tied to bulk band topology through bulk-edge correspondence. In photonic pseudospin-Hall systems, these states exhibit pseudospin-momentum locking, with lattice interactions and interface geometry determining each pseudospin's propagation direction. Reversing the pseudospin-dependent propagation direction without altering the lattice configuration or excitation handedness remains a fundamental challenge in controlling topological edge transport. Here, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate cavity-tunable topological edge transport in a microwave metasurface embedded within a metallic cavity. Varying the cavity height reshapes resonator interactions, driving band inversion and topological phase transition while preserving the lattice geometry. For a fixed domain-wall configuration, this transition reverses the propagation direction associated with each pseudospin while preserving pseudospin-momentum locking. Excitations with the same handedness are observed to launch edge waves propagating in opposite directions at their respective edge-band frequencies determined by the cavity height. These results establish cavity electrodynamics as an external means of controlling the bulk topology and reconfiguring the directional response of topological interfaces, creating new opportunities for topological wave routing in fixed photonic lattice structures.

items.title_en: Making Weak Interlayer Excitons Absorb: Manipulating the Effective Oscillator Strength via Purcell Engineering of Critical Coupling
items.title_zh: 使弱层间激子吸收：通过临界耦合的Purcell工程调控有效振子强度
items.abstract_en: Interlayer excitons (IXs) in transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers possess unique dipolar properties, providing a path for exploring correlated many-body phases, electrically tunable dipole-dipole interactions, and long-range exciton transport. However, the large electron-hole separation underlying their dipolar character also results in a significantly reduced oscillator strength, limiting their direct optical interaction with light, and thus the direct probing of their dynamics and many-body interactions. Here, we show that by using Purcell engineering of critical coupling, a weak interlayer transition can absorb as strongly as the dominant intralayer transition, despite its much smaller intrinsic oscillator strength. Using this approach, in an open cavity architecture we demonstrate an order of magnitude IX absorption modulation in bilayer and trilayer MoS2, with doubling of the IX to A-exciton interaction strength weight from ~23% to ~53%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in a tailored closed cavity architecture, the IX enhancement can reach beyond an order of magnitude, from ~5% to ~83% excitonic absorption, enabling IX absorption similar to intralayer excitons. An analytical description of the interaction is obtained via a closed-form transmission-line model which separates the excitonic and photonic contributions to the optical response, revealing how cavity architecture can be designed towards critical coupling. Our findings establish Purcell engineering of critical coupling as a general route to controlling and enhancing weak excitonic transitions.

items.title_en: Gaussian and Qubit Semigroup Dynamics beyond GKSL
items.title_zh: 超越GKSL的高斯与量子比特半群动力学
items.abstract_en: A well established approach to describe open quantum system dynamics is the celebrated Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation. In this article we aim to shed light on semigroup dynamics that are not of this form. Such dynamics may appear in real physical systems describing asymptotic long-time dynamics. Thus, they correspond to semigroup dynamics applicable to a restricted set of initial states only. As a way of motivating our studies, first we review known results about the single-mode Gaussian Quantum Brownian motion channel and corresponding master equations. Next we discuss a conceptually simpler family of qubit semigroup generators and identify parameter regions of completely positive, merely positive, and non-positive dynamics. We then focus on the latter case to which we will refer to as restricted-positive, as the semigroup generator may well be physically meaningful when applied to a restricted set of admissible initial states.

items.title_en: Photoacoustic-guided reflection-mode wavefront shaping through dynamic biological tissue
items.title_zh: 光声引导的反射式波前整形穿透动态生物组织
items.abstract_en: Strong optical scattering limits the depth at which light can be focused and used for imaging in biological tissue. Photoacoustic (PA)-guided wavefront shaping enables non-invasive light focusing in scattering media, but most existing implementations require optical and acoustic access from opposite sides of the sample and a rigidly aligned free-space optical path, which have confined these demonstrations to thin or static samples. Here, we combine a real-valued intensity transmission matrix (RVITM) algorithm with a photoacoustic guidestar (PA-RVITM) in a reflection-mode configuration. Modulated light is delivered through a flexible multimode fiber passing through the central aperture of a focused ultrasound transducer, enabling optical illumination and acoustic detection from the same side of the sample without a free-space combiner. Fiber integration preserved the wavefront shaping performance, and the reflection-mode PA-RVITM system achieved sub-second wavefront optimization with a ~14-fold PA signal enhancement through a diffuser. In ex vivo chicken breast tissue, the enhancement decreased with tissue thickness, reaching ~3.5 through a 2-mm chicken breast layer, with a speckle decorrelation time of ~450 ms. By performing an independent RVITM optimization at each scan position, our system enabled photoacoustic microscopy of a black nylon wire through the same layer, reducing the imaged line width from ~141 μm to ~102 μm, close to the nominal diameter of ~100 μm. This work advances PA-guided wavefront shaping toward a compact, same-side implementation for future biomedical therapeutic and imaging applications.

items.title_en: A hybrid quantum interferometer bridging Hong-Ou-Mandel and N00N-state interference
items.title_zh: 桥接Hong-Ou-Mandel与N00N态干涉的混合量子干涉仪
items.abstract_en: Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference offers robustness in high-noise environments due to its phase-insensitive nature, while N00N-state interference provides enhanced phase sensitivity for precision measurements in low-noise settings. However, their realizations have typically required separate experimental platforms. Here, we report a single hybrid quantum interferometer that can dynamically transition between HOM and N00N-state interference by adjusting two time delays, $τ_1$ and $τ_2$. This tunability enables operation in phase-insensitive, phase-sensitive, or hybrid modes within a unified setup, as confirmed by theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration. Our system offers a versatile platform with potential for quantum sensing applications, paving the way for integrated quantum technologies capable of adapting to diverse noise conditions.

items.title_en: Geometric-resource bounds and permutation-averaged success probabilities for the WZP algorithm
items.title_zh: WZP算法的几何资源界与置换平均成功概率
items.abstract_en: Solving linear systems of equations is a fundamental task in machine learning and optimization. In this work, we extend the original WZP algorithm from real symmetric linear systems to complex Hermitian linear systems. We then study the success probability of the modified WZP algorithm from a resource-theoretic perspective. By expressing the postselection success probability as the expectation value of a positive operator, we derive upper and lower bounds of the maximal success probability over separable, incoherent, and real pure states. These bounds further establish connections between the maximal success probability and geometric entanglement, coherence, and imaginarity. We further show that, under permutation averaging, the averaged success probability is an affine function of the coherence fraction, with its dependence determined by the alignment between the success operator and the equal-superposition state. We also investigate the preprocessed WZP algorithm under subgroup-constrained preprocessing. For the two-level family, the optimal success probability is determined by the maximal projection weight onto the orbit of the target projector. Our results provide a unified perspective on the WZP success probability under different operational constraints.

items.title_en: From Single-Particle Thermal Asymmetry to Collective Control: Janus Plasmonic Colloids for Photothermal Applications
items.title_zh: 从单粒子热不对称性到集体控制：用于光热应用的Janus等离子体胶体
items.abstract_en: Janus nanoheaters provide a route to break the spatial symmetry of thermoplasmonic heating and generate directionally biased thermal gradients at the nanoscale. However, in realistic photothermal scenarios, nanoheaters rarely act as isolated objects, but rather operate within colloidal assemblies where collective thermal and electromagnetic effects reshape the local temperature landscape. Here, we investigate how the intrinsic thermal asymmetry of a single Janus plasmonic nanoheater is transformed when moving from isolated particles to planar random arrays under continuous-wave illumination. Using coupled electromagnetic and steady-state heat-transfer simulations, we first quantify the finite spatial range over which the single-particle Janus signature remains detectable. We show that neighboring nanoheaters introduce two competing effects: a nearly symmetric collective thermal background that screens and homogenizes the Janus factor, and short-range neighbor-induced asymmetries that partially compensate this screening when interparticle distances become comparable to the spatial extent of the single-particle thermal anisotropy. We derive a closed-form analytical model for the array-averaged Janus factor as a function of nanoparticle number and surface density. The model predicts the screening-dominated regime from single-particle quantities and identifies deviations associated with near-field neighbor-induced contributions at higher densities. These results demonstrate a central trade-off for biomedical photothermal applications in continuous-wave operation: collective heating is required to reach relevant temperature increments, but it progressively erases the directional Janus character by thermal homogenization. Our framework provides a practical route to predict and rationally design the spatial temperature distribution in plasmonic assemblies of Janus particles.

items.title_en: Quantized six-vertex realizations of frustration graphs
items.title_zh: 阻挫图的量子化六顶点实现
items.abstract_en: A recent graph-theoretic criterion for a Hamiltonian to exhibit a free-parafermion spectrum is that its frustration graph be an indifference graph. We show that an arbitrary finite indifference graph can be realized as a frustration graph of the quantized six-vertex model at odd roots of unity, by a suitable choice of the defining wiring diagram and parameters. This provides a concrete realization of the criterion through the quantum Frobenius property of the quantized six-vertex model, recently established from its three-dimensional integrable structure.

items.title_en: Exact analytical spectra of an effective field-modified radial Schrödinger equation by the Nikiforov--Uvarov method
items.abstract_en: We revisit the effective radial Schrödinger equation for a charged spinless particle in collinear static electric and magnetic fields that was formulated in our earlier work within the tridiagonal representation approach (TRA). In that model the angular factor of the electric coupling is replaced by the orientation parameter $C=\cosθ$, the linear Zeeman term is diagonal in the azimuthal quantum number, and the effective field-modified central potential takes the form $V(r)=\Vt(r)+qECr$. Here we show that the same equation can be solved exactly without the TRA, by the Nikiforov--Uvarov (NU) method, once the potential component $\Vt(r)$ is prescribed. Three examples are worked out in closed form: a Kratzer-type component, which yields a linear-plus-Coulomb-plus-inverse-square central potential; a pseudoharmonic-type component, which yields a linear-plus-harmonic-plus-inverse-square potential; and a Hulthén-type component with a repulsive core (Manning--Rosen form), which yields a screened confining potential with a finite number of $s$-wave bound states. For each case we obtain the energy spectrum, the normalized eigenfunctions in terms of Laguerre or Jacobi polynomials, the location of the potential minimum, and closed-form radial moments. The spectra are independent of the orientation $θ$ and of the electric field, in agreement with the structure found by the TRA, while the field enters through the shape of $V(r)$, the radial moments, and the expectation value $\langle V\rangle_k$. All analytical results are confirmed by an independent finite-difference diagonalization.

items.title_en: Pinning of a High-Energy Wavepacket by a Single Impurity
items.abstract_en: We demonstrate that a single repulsive impurity enhances directional confinement of a high-energy wavepacket in a finite two-dimensional lattice of quantum wells. At energies far above the interwell barriers, the impurity suppresses transverse dynamical tunneling while preserving propagation along a principal lattice axis, even as the corresponding classical regular region shrinks. Confinement is strongest at impurity amplitudes comparable to the barrier height and weakens for stronger perturbations. Spectral analysis links this nonmonotonic pinning to the wavepacket's overlap with eigenstates concentrated along the launch direction, consistent with impurity-induced variational scarring. These results show that a single local defect can control quantum propagation over distances far exceeding its own spatial extent.

items.title_en: Directional effects of the Unruh effect on steering harvesting
items.abstract_en: We investigate directional quantum steering harvesting by two uniformly accelerated non-identical Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We show that the Unruh effect does not simply degrade harvested steering, but can reshape its directionality in a strongly parameter-dependent manner. At low detector energy scales, acceleration predominantly suppresses steering, whereas at higher energy scales, moderate acceleration can enhance steering and even activate an initially absent steering direction. Most strikingly, within a finite acceleration window, the Unruh effect enhances steering in one direction while simultaneously suppressing it in the opposite direction, revealing an intrinsically directional influence of relativistic acceleration. Detector non-identicality provides an additional control mechanism: a moderate energy-gap mismatch can enhance or activate one steering direction while suppressing the reverse one, whereas sufficiently large energy-gap mismatch suppresses the harvested steering. Moreover, the maximal steering asymmetry approximately marks the transition from two-way to one-way steering. Our results establish relativistic acceleration and detector non-identicality as means of controlling the strength and directionality of vacuum-harvested quantum correlations.

items.title_en: Loss-Tolerant Measurement-Device-Independent QKD over Untrusted Repeaters via High-Dimensional Time-Bin Multiplexing
items.abstract_en: We propose a loss-tolerant measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) protocol using time-bin-multiplexed single photons entangled with local qubits stored in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers. In each round, Alice and Bob each send a single multiplexed photon to an untrusted intermediary, Charlie. Each photon first becomes entangled with Charlie's NV-center qubits; Charlie then performs entanglement swapping between his NV qubits to establish EPR pairs between Alice's and Bob's local qubits. With $d$ time bins per photon, $\log_2 d + 1$ EPR pairs can be generated per transmitted photon, substantially increasing the probability of EPR-pair creation under limited channel bandwidth. To further mitigate the effects of prolonged memory storage, the protocol employs a memory-insensitive (MI) architecture, where multiple banks of qubits and multiplexed photon routing reduce the effective memory lifetime requirements. This approach enhances loss tolerance, enabling higher secret key rates and secure key distribution over longer distances compared to conventional single-photon protocols. Using the Lo-Chau EPR-QKD framework and Shor-Preskill reduction, we prove that the protocol is secure without trusting intermediate nodes, making it suitable for quantum networks with untrusted repeaters.

items.title_en: A low-cost compact muon detector for millikelvin operation
items.abstract_en: Ionizing radiation produces correlated errors in superconducting qubits, posing some challenges to quantum error correction. In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Cosmic muons are a component of this background that can only be partly shielded against at ground level, but can be tagged by an independent detector inside the cryostat, so that the affected data can be vetoed, or the muon tags incorporated into error correction. We present a low-cost, compact muon detector consisting of two plastic scintillator modules, each read out by a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), operated in coincidence. We characterize the SiPMs from room temperature down to 10 mK, including the breakdown and upper-limit voltages that define the operating bias range. Operated as a muon counter, the detector measures a coincidence rate that, as expected, is independent of temperature within uncertainties and agrees with analytical and Monte Carlo predictions. Below approximately 8 K, each muon event produces two pulses, one narrow and one broad, an effect that, to our knowledge, has not been reported before. Coincidences with an independent muon detector outside the cryostat confirm that muons are still counted reliably in this regime. By studying the appearance of double pulses as a function of temperature and magnetic field up to 4.5 T, we find a behavior consistent with the phase diagram of a type-II superconductor. This links the double pulses to a superconducting material in the SiPM, likely an adhesion layer or diffusion barrier introduced during manufacturing. The mechanism by which the superconducting state produces the second pulse is not yet understood.

items.title_en: Near-field contributions to cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer
items.abstract_en: Embedding materials in optical cavities has emerged as a powerful strategy for controlling their physical properties. In this context, increasing attention has been devoted to the thermal Purcell effect, which describes how the radiative heat transfer between a material and its photonic environ- ment can be modified by the electromagnetic boundary conditions imposed by the cavity. Here, we investigate near-field effects in cavity-mediated radiative heat transfer in planar cavities composed of realistic, dissipative gold mirrors, extending previous work that considered ideal mirrors. We iden- tify the conditions under which near-field effects lead to a substantial enhancement of heat transfer between the material and a photonic thermal bath relative to free space, owing to the strong modi- fication of the photonic local density of states by evanescent modes within the cavity. In particular, we find that radiative heat flow can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude in cavities ranging from nanometer to micrometer scales, depending on the absorber frequency and dipole orientation. These findings suggest that near-field effects may be relevant to polariton chemistry experiments and other systems operating within this cavity length-scale regime. Our results add to the idea that cavities can modify material properties not only by engineering vacuum fluctuations in the strong light-matter coupling regime, but also by controlling radiative dissipation and heat transfer.

items.title_en: Polaritonic self-hybridized critical coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
items.abstract_en: Maximizing the absorption of exciton-polaritons in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) under critical coupling conditions is crucial for developing high-efficiency polariton-based photodetectors, solar cells, and perfect absorbers. Here, we propose a polaritonic critical self-hybridized coupling between Brillouin zone folding driven quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBIC) mode and A excitons in a bulk WS2 metasurface. This polaritonic critical coupling shows robust behavior with respect to the asymmetric parameters of the involved BZF-QBIC mode, in contrast to the asymmetry-sensitive conventional QBIC-based critical coupling. By changing the height of WS2 metasurfaces, we observe a typical anti-crossing behavior with a Rabi splitting of 246.5 meV. Moreover, the maximum absorption value of 0.5 for exciton-polaritons is achieved at the polaritonic critical coupling condition. The large population of excitons provided by bulk WS2 is essential for achieving polaritonic critical coupling and can further enhance polaritonic absorption. This work enables the realization of robust, high-absorption self-hybridized polaritonic critical coupling in TMDCs, and further expedite their applications in high-absorption low-dimensional polaritonic devices.

items.title_en: Strong subadditivity of topological entropy on the torus: Rényi order and non-Abelian structure
items.abstract_en: We classify strong subadditivity for the canonical topological Rényi functional at finite positive orders on an unpunctured torus in the topological quantum field theory of any finite unitary modular tensor category. Universal validity means validity for all pure ground states and all regular region pairs with transverse or disjoint boundaries and compatible corner rounding. At von Neumann order one, the inequality holds universally. For each fixed order strictly between zero and one, universal validity is equivalent to pointedness, meaning that every simple anyon type has quantum dimension one. For every nonpointed category and each finite positive order other than one, we construct a violating pure state and an allowed pair. For a fixed pointed category and fixed order above one, universal validity is equivalent to a same-order modular Fourier entropy bound for every pure state. Global homological constraints on actual unions and intersections and established weighted modular uncertainty prove the order-one theorem. For parallel annuli at fixed flux distribution, the order-one functional is affine in their positive count. At other orders, unequal quantum dimensions on the occupied support induce strict curvature that suitable overlapping regions convert into negative deficits. Under the boundary-charge cutting prescription, the von Neumann theorem extends to arbitrary logical density matrices in the same ground space.

items.title_en: Sorption Molecular Dynamics of Point Defects in 2D Materials with a Machine Learning Potential
items.title_zh: 基于机器学习势的二维材料点缺陷吸附分子动力学
items.abstract_en: Defect engineering is a crucial tool for tuning and tailoring the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials. A key challenge is identifying which defects are kinetically stable at room temperature and sufficiently promising to warrant further investigation. However, identifying stable defects with suitable properties using first-principles calculations, such as density functional theory (DFT) is computationally demanding, effectively limiting the scope of high-throughput studies. In this work, we investigate whether the machine learning interatomic potential MACE can reproduce sorption trends (adsorption vs. absorption) previously obtained from high-throughput DFT calculations and extend the analysis to elevated temperatures. A total of 17,624 defect structures from the ADAQ database are simulated using MACE-accelerated molecular dynamics (MD) at both 0 K and 300 K. The results show that MACE successfully reproduces the overall sorption trends observed in DFT calculations at 0 K at a fraction of the computational cost. Simulations performed at 300 K further indicate that the qualitative sorption trends remain largely the same when including finite-temperature effects. These findings demonstrate that MACE-driven MD can be used as an effective high-throughput prescreening tool for defect-related studies in 2D materials, specially related to sorption. While conventional first-principles methods, such as DFT, remain necessary for accurate and quantitative validation, the use of MLIPs enables MD simulations of finite-temperature defect behavior at a fraction of the computational cost of DFT-based MD.

items.title_en: Dicke model of open-shell atoms with tensor polarizability
items.abstract_en: We study the extended Dicke model obtained from the scalar--vector--tensor polarizability of open-shell atoms coupled to a shared cavity mode. For a single electric-dipole channel, rotational symmetry fixes the tensor to vector ratio; we use $^{168}\mathrm{Er}$ with $J=6$ as a product-state example. A circular pump produces a chiral Raman vertex whose tensor-dependent matrix elements select the occupied Zeeman sector. The resulting first-order transition occurs before the empty-cavity branch loses local stability, and the ordered state is read out through $\langle\hat J_z\rangle$. A linear pump instead produces an empty-cavity $\pm x$ cat and a continuous transition into an even-$m$ cat-like state with order parameter $\langle\hat J_z^2\rangle$. With cavity loss alone, the circular trajectory emits a photon burst and approaches a Raman-dark Zeeman pole rather than a finite-field condensate. In the linear geometry, cavity-bright modes are damped toward the cat-like branch while a dark spin mode remains undamped. These are phenomena of that model; the vector-only controls show that they depend on the channel-fixed tensor coupling.

items.title_en: Advances in quantum optomechanical control based on cavity cold-atom systems
items.abstract_en: Cavity optomechanics represents a frontier research direction in quantum science and technology, centered on the control and exploration of interactions between electromagnetic fields and mechanical motion. Rooted in quantum mechanics, this field realizes efficient coupling and precise manipulation of optical fields and mechanical vibrations through the structural design and precise regulation of optical microcavities and mechanical oscillators, thereby revealing and harnessing novel quantum phenomena. In recent years, cavity optomechanics has evolved into an interdisciplinary frontier integrating quantum optics, condensed matter physics, and quantum precision measurement, exhibiting profound application in both fundamental physics research and quantum information science. With advancements in technologies such as nanomanufacturing and laser cooling, optomechanical interactions have been successfully demonstrated in various experimental systems. Among these platforms, cavity cold-atom systems stand out as one of the ideal platforms for implementing quantum optomechanics. Featuring exceptional environmental isolation, long quantum coherence times, and strong light-matter interaction, these systems provide a crucial testbed for exploring strong and even ultrastrong optomechanical coupling effects as well as rich nonlinear quantum phenomena. This paper reviews the recent progress in optomechanical control and manipulation based on cavity cold-atom systems. We first outline the fundamental principles of standard cavity optomechanical systems. Then, we describe the experimental realization of linear and nonlinear optomechanical couplings in cold-atom systems. After that, we focus on the representative applications of this platform in high-precision quantum sensing, quantum memory, and the preparation of macroscopic nonclassical states. Finally, we give an outlook and challenges in this field.

items.title_en: Bias-Modulated Electronically-Tunable Optoelectronic Chromatic Dispersion in Ge PN Photodiodes
items.title_zh: Ge PN 光电二极管中偏压调制的电可调光电色散
items.abstract_en: Optoelectronic Chromatic Dispersion (OED) is a source of significant wavelength-dependent current in photodiodes, offering a pathway to computational spectroscopy in a photodiode-only platform without the need for additional optical or mechanical components. Previous studies have activated OED through light modulation. Here, we present a theoretical and experimental investigation of bias-modulated OED in the C- and L-bands in a Ge PN photodiode, where the applied bias voltage is modulated sinusoidally, and the optical illumination is held constant. The spectral response is due to wavelength-dependent optical absorption together with bias-dependent competition between carrier drift, displacement current, and mobile-charge screening. With the RF phase-shift technique, the maximum measured OED sensitivity is +4.13 deg/nm in the L-band, significantly larger than that of light-modulated OED in Ge. The 15 mdeg phase-noise floor yields a spectral resolution of 3.6 pm. These results establish bm-OED as an electronically reconfigurable dispersive mechanism for applications in chip-scale computational spectrometers, photonic integrated circuits (PICs), on-chip RF photonics, and wavelength-division multiplexing.

items.title_en: Metric-Changing Quasi-Hermitian Quenches: Normalized Loschmidt Amplitude and Complex-Time Zeros
items.abstract_en: In quasi-Hermitian mixed-state quenches, the initial and final Hamiltonians generally possess different positive-definite metrics, so post-quench evolution is not quasi-unitary in the initial physical space. Choosing the preparation/measurement space as reference, we derive from first principles a normalized mixed-state Loschmidt amplitude using metric-compatible purifications. The resulting biorthogonal trace representation contains a normalization factor given by the norm of the evolved purification in the initial metric; this factor is essential for comparing states from different physical Hilbert spaces and directly encodes the metric mismatch. We prove that this normalization function is strictly positive on the real-time axis, so real-time criticality arises solely from destructive interference in the dynamical overlap. In complex time, zeros of the normalization factor generate branch singularities distinct from Fisher zeros. For a general two-level system, we derive analytic expressions for the Fisher and normalization zeros and analyze exceptional-point scaling together with the temperature- and quasi-Hermiticity-dependent DQPT critical times in two solvable quench protocols. In contrast to metric-stationary quenches, where non-Hermitian effects may be absorbed into an equivalent Hermitian description, the metric mismatch here produces genuine non-Hermitian dynamics: a time-dependent normalization factor and complex-time branch structure that cannot be removed by any global similarity transformation.

items.title_en: Multi-Instantons and Exact-WKB Stokes Jumps in Multi-Well Quantum Mechanics
items.abstract_en: We study the relation between the exact-WKB Delabaere--Dillinger--Pham Stokes jumps and the multi-instanton expansion of a one-dimensional potential with $N$ equal-depth minima. For a single barrier this relation is the Bogomolny--Zinn-Justin cancellation between the instanton--anti-instanton ambiguity and the Borel ambiguity of perturbation theory, and we extend it to every consecutive barrier interval and to the integration contours themselves. In the dilute large-$T$ regime at fixed nonperturbative grade, we derive the quasi-zero mode integral over the instanton separations from the Euclidean path integral and reduce it to Gamma and Hankel periods. With the local Weber level function of each well and one normalization per well fixed by the local Weber connection matrix, these periods reproduce the two lateral connected exact-WKB coefficients. The two lateral contours of each instanton--anti-instanton separation differ by exactly one Hankel cycle, and this linear Picard--Lefschetz relation reproduces the Stokes jump of the connected coefficient. A numerical solution of the Schrödinger equation for a symmetric triple well confirms the resulting two-barrier level splitting. At higher fixed grade, the map from ordered event sequences to normalized scalar coefficient products is not one-to-one. At leading dilute order the scalar weight of a closed event sequence depends only on the numbers of barrier crossings, $\mathcal I\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs, and $\mathcal I\mathcal I$/$\bar{\mathcal I}\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs. We construct two inequivalent grade-six triple-well event sequences with the same product of local Weber amplitudes, which embed in every potential with $N\ge3$ wells. Our results hold within the regular dilute, one-loop, local Weber approximation.

items.title_en: Hyperentanglement in intermediate phase-space planes: benchmarking a photon-pair source for quantum key distribution
items.abstract_en: We characterize a source of photon pairs simultaneously entangled in polarization and in the transverse spatial degree of freedom, with the spatial measurements performed in intermediate planes of the fractional Fourier transform. The source consists of two crossed type-I crystals in a non-collinear geometry, such that the transverse variables carry information about the crystal of origin. Detection in the crystal plane reveals this information completely and destroys the polarization entanglement, so that a scheme using the near and far fields as conjugate spatial bases cannot support a parallel polarization channel. In intermediate planes both spatial bases combine position and momentum, such that the which-crystal information is partially erased, and the polarization entanglement survives in all four combinations of spatial bases. Applying Bell and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen criteria to the same photon pairs certifies both degrees of freedom simultaneously. We evaluate quantum bit error rates and asymptotic secret key rates in each degree of freedom, and find that the source delivers two simultaneously usable channels per photon pair.

items.title_en: Inferring Transition-Dipoles from Two-Dimensional Infrared Spectroscopy with Deep Learning
items.title_zh: 利用深度学习从二维红外光谱推断跃迁偶极
items.abstract_en: Two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy is a powerful nonlinear technique for probing vibrational couplings, anharmonicities, coherence, and molecular dynamics. Among the microscopic parameters encoded in 2D IR spectra, transition dipoles are fundamental quantities that characterize molecular structure and govern light-matter interactions. However, reconstructing these quantities from spectroscopic data remains a challenging inverse problem. Here, we introduce a physics-informed convolutional neural network (CNN), Spec2DipoleNet, trained on 2D IR spectra generated via the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian (NHH) method. This multi-task CNN reconstructs the transition dipole matrices under physically-motivated masking constraints. On the validation set, the model achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.085, an $R^2$ of 0.97, and a normalized cross-correlation of 0.98. It reliably recovers matrix elements associated with allowed transitions, while larger deviations are observed for nominally forbidden transitions. Our results suggest that transition dipole operators can be quantitatively inferred from 2D IR spectra, highlighting the potential of physics-informed deep learning for extracting microscopic quantum parameters from multidimensional spectroscopic data.

items.title_en: Preservation of photon statistics upon selective molecular modulation in hollow-core fibers
items.abstract_en: Preserving the underlying statistical properties of light during frequency transduction is essential for interfacing spectrally disparate quantum systems. To do this successfully, the process needs to be highly efficient, broadband and noiseless. Despite significant progress in this field, satisfying all these conditions remains challenging. Recently, molecular modulation-based transduction in hollow-core fibers has emerged as a promising approach, where biphoton correlations were proven to be preserved during frequency up-conversion.
