However, beyond this previous demonstration of correlation-maintaining conversion, whether molecular modulation can preserve more general statistical properties of light remains experimentally unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the conservation of photon-number statistics during selective frequency transduction by Raman molecular modulation in a hydrogen-filled hollow-core fiber. As a proof of concept, weak 585-nm signals are selectively converted to 773 nm in the near-infrared and to 471 nm in the blue spectral region with near-unity efficiencies. Phase matching between the generated coherence waves and the transitions of interest is achieved through the effective dispersion of the system, enabling independent selection of the frequency up- and down-conversion processes. The preservation of the photon-number statistics of the shifted signals, along with the large frequency shifts, broad tunability and compatibility with quantum-optical fields, provides a versatile fiber-based platform for quantum frequency transduction. In particular, the demonstrated interfacing between visible and near-infrared wavelengths using low pump energies and low gas pressures offers a route towards connecting spectrally distinct quantum systems, including quantum emitters, sensors and atomic quantum memories, within hybrid quantum networks.

items.title_en: Testing graph isomorphism using simple quantum circuits
items.abstract_en: The graph isomorphism problem asks whether two graphs are equivalent up to a permutation of their vertices. Its precise computational complexity remains unresolved, and it is still unknown whether a polynomial-time algorithm exists. We investigate whether simple graph-dependent Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-time (IQP) and Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) circuits can distinguish non-isomorphic graphs. We first show that suitable IQP and QAOA constructions allow the underlying graph to be reconstructed using a polynomial number of samples. Building on previous work using the QAOA energy, we show that Hamming weight distributions can distinguish graph pairs at circuit depths for which the numerically computed energy gap is zero. We then apply graph invariants to the matrix of ZZ correlators on the output distribution. For the specific case of the graph spectrum, at QAOA depth $p=2$, this invariant numerically distinguishes all $10{,}486$ cospectral regular graph pairs tested on up to 18 vertices. For IQP circuits, we introduce a finer invariant based on probability multiplicities within Hamming weight sectors, which distinguishes every non-isomorphic graph pair tested numerically. Finally, we derive exact graph-theoretic characterisations of the IQP output distribution at $θ=π/2$ and $θ=π/4$. These results show that simple graph-dependent quantum circuits encode substantial structural information, while leaving open whether this information can be extracted efficiently for general graph isomorphism.

items.title_en: Observation of correlations beyond the single-particle picture in fermionic counting statistics
items.abstract_en: The analysis of charge fluctuations in a mesoscopic device can shed light on the fundamental question of whether or not a single-particle picture of electron transport is appropriate, even in the presence of Coulomb interaction. It has been shown on general grounds that mapping the interacting system onto a fermionic single-particle description is subject to strict constraints on the charge-transfer statistics. These constraints can be formulated in terms of a sign rule for the factorial cumulants of the full counting statistics. We report here on the experimental observation of a sign-rule violation in a most elementary model system, i.e. a single-level quantum dot, and provide theoretical modeling that can quantitatively reproduce the experimental data. This reveals the presence of correlations introduced by electron-electron interaction.

items.title_en: Joint-measurement advantage and finite-time transitions in accelerated detector registers
items.abstract_en: The Unruh response thermalizes accelerated detectors, but the entanglement remaining in a register does not by itself specify what distributed measurements can recover. We study this distinction for a four-qubit cluster state whose two assisting nodes independently undergo generalized amplitude damping, while the target nodes remain isolated and the environments are inaccessible. We derive the exact joint-assisted concurrence and the exact one-way value for arbitrary local measurements. The joint optimum equals the bipartition negativity, and computational-basis measurements attain the one-way optimum. A polar-decomposition argument, together with compactness, establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for separable measurements to attain the joint optimum and proves a strict gap whenever this condition fails. For assisting detectors at equal Unruh temperature with relaxation-rate ratio $r>1$, joint advantage exists precisely when the thermal excitation factor satisfies $q<1/r$. At finite positive temperature it ends at a unique finite time, while the remaining entanglement is nonzero. For $r=2$, both the transition time and remaining resource have closed expressions. These results identify when joint assistance is necessary within the independent weak-coupling thermalization model.

items.title_en: Improved Quantum Algorithms for Rényi Entropies Estimation
items.abstract_en: Entropy estimation of discrete probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistical inference and quantum property estimation. In this paper, we study the problem of estimating Rényi entropy $H_α(\mathbf{p})$ for any distribution $\mathbf{p} = (p_i)_{i=1}^n$ given its purified quantum query-access. For non-integer $α> 1$, our algorithm estimates $H_α(\mathbf{p})$ to within additive error $ε$ using only $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{\max\{1/2,1-1/α\}}/ε\big)$ queries, which improves the best known upper bound for dependence on both $n$ and $1/ε$. For $0<α<1$, our algorithm has query complexity $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(n^{1/(2α)}/ε^{\max\{1,1/(2α)\}}\big)$, which improves the dependence on $1/ε$ of the current best upper bound without incresing its $n$ dependence. Our approach adapts the multi-level estimation framework to relative approximation of the power sums and leverage binary search to remove the requirement of prior knowledge of them. We also strengthen the precision-dependent lower bound to $Ω\big(1/ε^{\max\{1,1/(2α)\}}\big)$ for $0<α<1$, which identifies the optimal precision dependence of our algorithm.

items.title_en: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation
items.title_zh: LatentLoop：以非对称算力分配扩展循环 MoE 模型
items.abstract_en: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models combine parameter reuse with sparse computation to improve performance under matched budgets. Prior work demonstrates that different loop visits can play different roles even when they share parameters. To probe the contributions of different loop visits, we learn separate residual coefficients in a model that applies a shared block twice, observing a smaller scale in the first visit. Fixed coefficient experiments show that reducing the first visit's scale preserves or improves performance, whereas the same reductions to the second hurt it. This asymmetry motivates us to explore asymmetric compute allocation. We propose \textbf{LatentLoop}, which compresses the first visit's sequence, retains full resolution in the second, and reallocates saved computation to increase the hidden size. We further learn how strongly the first visit updates the full sequence, and share MoE weights across visits while using separate attention parameters to accommodate their different sequence resolutions. Across 15 configurations spanning 1.3B--7B parameters, with the largest budget exceeding $10^{21}$ FLOPs, LatentLoop consistently lowers validation NLL. At a fitted NLL of 1.988, predicted compute savings are 19.0\% and 7.9\% relative to vanilla MoE and the looped baseline. It also improves average scores on nine benchmarks at all sizes in 0-shot and 5-shot settings. These results suggest asymmetric compute allocation is a promising direction for looped MoE models.
items.abstract_zh: 循环式专家混合（MoE）模型把参数复用与稀疏计算结合起来，在同等预算下提升性能。已有工作表明，即使共享参数，不同的循环访问也可以扮演不同角色。为探究各次访问的贡献，我们在一个将共享块应用两次的模型中分别学习残差系数，观察到第一次访问的尺度更小。固定系数实验显示，减小第一次访问的尺度可保持甚至提升性能，而对第二次作同样缩减则有害。这种不对称促使我们探索非对称算力分配，并提出 LatentLoop：压缩第一次访问的序列，第二次保持全分辨率，并把节省下的计算重新分配给增大隐藏维度。我们还学习第一次访问对全序列的更新强度，并在两次访问间共享 MoE 权重、使用各自独立的注意力参数以适配不同的序列分辨率。在 1.3B–7B 参数、最大预算超过 10^21 FLOPs 的 15 种配置上，LatentLoop 一致降低验证 NLL；在拟合 NLL 为 1.988 处，预计相对普通 MoE 与循环基线分别节省 19.0% 与 7.9% 的计算。在 0-shot 与 5-shot 设置下，它在全部规模的九个基准上平均分均有所提升。
items.highlight_zh: 前段压缩、后段全分辨率：非对称算力分配更省算力且NLL更低
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究问题：循环 MoE 模型通过多次复用同一套参数、配合稀疏专家计算来提升性能。此前工作发现不同“循环访问”扮演不同角色，但没弄清每次访问到底贡献什么，也没系统利用这种差异来省算力。
2) 方法：先做诊断——在共享块被应用两次的模型里，给两次访问分别学习残差系数，结果第一次访问的系数明显更小；固定系数的实验进一步证实，缩小第一次访问的尺度性能不降反升，而同样缩小第二次则明显变差。这种不对称说明算力不该平均分配。据此作者提出 LatentLoop：把第一次访问的序列压缩，第二次保持全分辨率，把省下来的算力用于加大隐藏维度；同时学习第一次访问对整条序列的更新强度，两次访问共享 MoE 权重但各用独立的注意力参数，以适配不同的序列分辨率。
3) 结果：在 1.3B–7B 参数、最大预算超过 10^21 FLOPs 的 15 种配置上，LatentLoop 的验证 NLL 一致更低；在拟合 NLL 为 1.988 处，预计相对普通 MoE 和循环基线分别节省约 19.0% 与 7.9% 的计算量。九个基准在 0-shot 和 5-shot 下、各规模的平均分均提升。
4) 意义：把“循环”从对称的重复变成有结构的非对称算力分配，为循环 MoE 的扩展提供了一条简单、可复用的设计原则，也说明循环各次访问的功能确实可以解耦。

items.title_en: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
items.title_zh: 以批评引导的在线策略蒸馏恢复可靠监督
items.abstract_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model on its own rollouts with token-level supervision from a teacher, assuming that the teacher can reach a correct answer from any prefix the student writes. We call this property the recoverability of the teacher and show it fails on incorrect rollouts: the teacher follows student errors, although it recognizes them. We propose CriticOPD, using error recognition to restore recoverability. The teacher critiques an incorrect rollout, allowing the student to rewrite its solution following the error. The resulting output, including the critique as privileged information, is scored by the teacher while the student uses the revision without the critique for training. On two Qwen3 students and six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, CriticOPD improves OPD, with the largest gains on competition problems.
items.abstract_zh: 在线策略蒸馏（OPD）让学生模型在自己的 rollout 上接受教师的 token 级监督，其隐含假设是：教师能从学生写出的任何前缀出发抵达正确答案。我们把这一性质称为教师的可恢复性，并表明它在错误 rollout 上会失效：教师虽然能识别错误，却仍会跟随学生的错误。我们提出 CriticOPD，利用错误识别来恢复可恢复性。教师先对错误 rollout 给出批评，使学生能在错误之后重写解答；由此得到的输出（把批评作为特权信息）由教师打分，而学生在训练时只使用不含批评的修订答案。在两个 Qwen3 学生模型和六个数学推理基准上，CriticOPD 相较 OPD 均有提升，在竞赛类题目上增益最大。
items.highlight_zh: 用教师批评纠正错误 rollout，恢复 OPD 监督的可靠性
items.digest_zh:
1) 研究问题：在线策略蒸馏（OPD）让学生在自己的采样轨迹（rollout）上接受教师的 token 级监督，其隐含前提是“教师能从学生写出的任意前缀出发走到正确答案”。作者把这一性质称为教师可恢复性，并指出它在学生出错时会失效：教师虽然能识别错误，却依然顺着学生的错误往下写，于是给出的监督信号本身并不可靠。
2) 方法：作者提出 CriticOPD，用“错误识别”来恢复可恢复性。具体做法是：教师先对错误的 rollout 给出批评，明确指出错在哪里，学生据此重写自己的解答；得到的新输出连同批评一起作为特权信息交给教师打分，而学生在训练时只使用“不含批评的修订答案”。这样教师不必从错误前缀硬推出正确答案，学生也能从示范中学到如何自我纠错。
3) 结果：在两个 Qwen3 学生模型、六个数学推理基准上，CriticOPD 相对原始 OPD 稳定提升，并且在竞赛类难题上增益最大——这正符合“出错更频繁、更需要纠错”的场景。
4) 意义：论文揭示了一个此前被忽视的 OPD 失效模式，并给出只改变监督构造、不改模型结构的简单修复方案；对于用强模型蒸馏推理能力的实际训练流程而言，这是一个低成本、可直接套用的改进。

items.title_en: Long-Horizon RL Needs Muon
items.title_zh: 长时程强化学习需要 Muon
items.abstract_en: Long-horizon agents must coordinate reasoning, tool use, and environment feedback over extended interactions. Learning from sparse outcome rewards requires weighting trajectories of different lengths and updating the policy while rollouts are still being collected. We examine a single-rollout asynchronous recipe combining Muon, token-averaged loss, truncated importance sampling, and auxiliary length and tool-error penalties. Single-rollout sampling allows asynchronous learning without waiting for multiple trajectories for the same issue. We study optimizer choices and recipe components for repository-level issue resolution across two model families. The evaluated training runs show higher training success with the full recipe than with the baselines.
items.abstract_zh: 长时程智能体必须在长时间交互中协调推理、工具调用与环境反馈。仅依赖稀疏结果奖励的学习，需要对不同长度的轨迹加权，并在 rollout 仍在收集时更新策略。我们考察一种单轨迹异步训练配方，它结合了 Muon 优化器、按 token 平均的损失、截断重要性采样，以及长度惩罚和工具错误惩罚等辅助项。单轨迹采样使异步学习无需等待同一问题的多条轨迹。我们在两个模型家族上研究仓库级问题修复任务中的优化器选择与配方组件。所评测的训练运行表明，使用完整配方的训练成功率高于基线。
items.highlight_zh: 单轨迹异步配方配 Muon，仓库级修复成功率更高
items.digest_zh: 1) 研究了什么问题：训练能连续调用工具、多轮推理并接收环境反馈的长时程智能体时，往往只有最终成败这一稀疏奖励，且轨迹长短不一，训练既慢又难。2) 用了什么方法：采用「单轨迹」异步训练流程——不必等同一问题采样出多条轨迹就能更新策略，并配合 Muon 优化器、按 token 平均的损失、截断重要性采样，另外加入长度惩罚与工具调用出错惩罚作为辅助信号。3) 有什么结果：在仓库级代码问题修复任务上，跨两个模型家族评测，使用完整配方的训练成功率高于各基线。4) 为何重要：它说明优化器（Muon）与这些训练组件在长时程异步强化学习中并非可有可无，为该类可扩展的智能体训练提供了一套实用可复现的配方。

items.title_en: The COUNT: Counting N-grams Unlocks Scaling on Host Memory and Training-Free Adaptation
items.title_zh: COUNT：N-gram计数解锁主机内存扩展与免训练适配
items.abstract_en: The scaling relationship of compute and performance for language models (LMs) has been extensively studied; more recently, models are being designed to scale memory use, as well. In particular, adding embeddings for n-grams scales memory separately from compute use, because each pass only processes individual embedding rows, which are much smaller than the storage used for the whole embedding table. However, existing methods train embeddings from scratch, which needs expensive GPU memory for fast reading and writing. Meanwhile, the ordinary memory of the host system is cheap and underutilized by these training methods. To scale on host memory, we introduce COUNT (Counting Offline Unlocks N-gram Transformers), which builds n-gram embeddings without adding learned parameters by storing precomputed n-gram counts on host. We use the corpus frequencies to weight together the LM's own unembeddings of the next tokens most often following the current n-gram history. At a fixed compute budget, COUNT can be added as an additional input embedding for pretraining 1B-parameter LMs to improve validation loss as much as an LM with 57% more compute. If GPU memory is limited, using COUNT to let backbone parameters fill GPU memory gives better performance than splitting memory with additional learned n-gram embeddings. Beyond efficiency, COUNT allows switching in a different table of n-gram counts from a domain-specific corpus at inference time to adapt to a new task without any training.

items.title_en: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
items.title_zh: 用扩散模型建模与理解人形机器人策略的神经网络权重
items.abstract_en: Recent advances in robot learning have driven rapid progress in humanoid control, enabling increasingly agile behaviors in the real world. However, humanoid control networks are typically obtained through conventional training procedures, while comparatively little attention has been given to directly modeling the distribution of their learned weights and generating functional networks in weight space. In this work, we investigate whether high-performing humanoid control networks can be generatively modeled directly through their weights. We adopt a latent diffusion framework that couples a linear autoencoder with a Diffusion Transformer. The autoencoder compresses actor network parameters into a compact latent space, and the Diffusion Transformer models the distribution of these latents. Trained on networks collected from reinforcement learning for the Unitree G1 robot, our approach generates deployable networks that perform various motions in the real world, including walking, dancing, and spin kick. Beyond generation, we further study the learned weight space to better understand the structure captured by these humanoid control networks. We identify a structural principle in the first-layer weights that consistently reflects the robot's kinematic prior. Notably, this kinematic prior emerges under both Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Imitation Learning (IL) training, suggesting that it is not specific to a particular optimization process but may instead reflect common knowledge associated with humanoid embodiment. Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of generative modeling in humanoid network weight space, while providing initial insights into the information encoded by their learned weights. Additional results are available on our project website: https://humanoid-weight-diffusion.github.io/

items.title_en: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
items.title_zh: 稀疏人类指导下的真实世界移动操作分层残差策略学习
items.abstract_en: Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) is a cornerstone of autonomous robotic systems, yet real-world fine-tuning remains a formidable challenge because of high-dimensional action spaces and intricate coupling between heterogeneous modules. In this paper, we propose HiRe-MoMa (Hierarchical Residual Mobile Manipulation), a systematic framework for stable and sample-efficient real-world fine-tuning of complex MoMa systems. At its core, HiRe-MoMa adopts a Hierarchical Residual Architecture that fine-tunes a frozen base policy. A Policy-Agnostic Residual learns additive corrections atop the base policy, while Hierarchical Decoupling splits the residual into mobile-base and manipulator-arm heads with unidirectional conditioning, mitigating gradient interference and aligning corrections with the platform's physical hierarchy. To improve sample efficiency in data-expensive real-world settings, we propose Expert-Guided Value Alignment, which leverages sparse human interventions with under 20% training coverage to reshape the critic's value landscape, effectively guiding autonomous exploration through expert priors. Extensive real-world experiments on the TIAGo++ platform demonstrate that HiRe-MoMa consistently enhances task performance with only around 30 minutes of online interaction, regardless of the base policy architecture. To our knowledge, this is among the first frameworks to enable efficient on-robot fine-tuning for mobile manipulation in the real world, providing a practical paradigm for deploying complex robotic systems in dynamic, human-centric environments. Further details can be found on our project website: https://hire-moma.github.io/

items.title_en: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
items.title_zh: 面向语言智能体的行动与预测协同进化
items.abstract_en:
Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused. Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response. Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step in the trajectory, and (2) observation targets, such as web pages and terminal logs, are long and noisy and reach only one step ahead. We propose 
ame, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets. On successful on-policy trajectories, 
ame trains the policy backbone to generate the action sequences that follows each history. Each action is also supervised when forecast from the preceding histories, forming a temporal ensemble that the shared backbone absorbs during training, and this enables acting and forecasting to co-evolve. The policy still acts one step at a time at inference, with no overhead. Across five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, $τ^2$-bench, and AppWorld), 
ame (1) achieves stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and RL baselines with predictive auxiliary targets across simulated environments, while improving overall performance on both realistic applications; (2) delivers up to $1.9	imes$ and $2.0	imes$ higher sample efficiency than ECHO and GRPO, respectively, on ScienceWorld; and (3) achieves these gains with a single policy backbone, without additional models, separate pretraining, or inference overhead. The codebase is available at https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/CoPE.

items.title_en: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
items.title_zh: 你的 Transformer 其实是弹性的
items.abstract_en: Scaling up transformers has produced models with broad capabilities, deployed across heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads. Yet, model families offer only a few fixed sizes (e.g., S, B, L), forcing users to commit to a model based on hardware and latency constraints. This rigidity is often suboptimal under varying query loads. We introduce a retraining-free method that elastifies pre-trained transformers into a single model that adapts on-the-fly across a continuum of computational budgets. Our key contribution is a differentiable relaxation of the functional unit-ranking problem: unlike prior work, which optimizes a single importance weight per MLP block or attention head, we rank every individual MLP neuron and attention head jointly, on a common scale, by minimizing the model's loss under soft pruning across many sparsity targets, all at once. Across 27 vision and text transformer encoders ranging from 22M to 8B parameters, our method yields smooth degradation up to 60% sparsity and outperforms one-shot baselines under deep pruning. For example, pruning DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 to 50% sparsity removes 427M parameters while reducing ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy by only 0.8%, without the need for weight correction or retraining. At 60% sparsity, a pruned AugReg ViT-B/16 model achieves up to $1.80\times$ higher throughput and $1.26\times$ lower single-query latency on an A100 GPU. Elastic models are produced in minutes, with construction time scaling sub-linearly with parameter count.

items.title_en: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets
items.title_zh: 智能体市场中第一价格拍卖的无政府状态代价
items.abstract_en: An agentic market is a decentralized serving-time market where AI agents bid to claim each user prompt. An agent's bid is based on its expected value for the prompt, which is the expectation of the reward for its response minus its inference costs. First-price auctions (FPAs), in which the highest bidder pays its bid and receives the prompt, are a natural way to allocate prompts in such a market, since they are simple and transparent to run, and do not require central knowledge of private capabilities and costs. However, FPAs are not truthful: participants may bid less than their true value in the hope of a larger profit, and the prompt may then be allocated to someone other than the bidder who values it the most. This welfare loss is quantified by the $\textit{price-of-anarchy}$ (PoA). In this paper, we argue that agentic markets are likely to possess features that reduce the price-of-anarchy. The first is a $\textit{competitive floor}$, which occurs when multiple bidders usually value the prompt above some baseline share of the optimal welfare (e.g., because the best models are often distilled into cheaper alternatives, which perform similarly). We show that competition among them then limits the welfare loss, which can be driven to zero as the floor rises. The second feature is $\textit{near-independence}$ of values after conditioning on the prompt, which occurs when most of the predictable variation in the expected value is determined by the difficulty of the prompt. As the value distribution approaches conditional independence, we can derive an efficiency guarantee that approaches a factor of $1 - 1/e^2$ of the optimal welfare. Thus, both features give rise to welfare lower bounds that are significantly better than the well-known general case of $1 - 1/e$. We validate these results empirically using auctions with strategic bidders simulated on the EmbedLLM prompt routing dataset.

items.title_en: Continuum Attention
items.title_zh: 连续统注意力
items.abstract_en: We introduce Continuum Attention (CA), a causal Transformer attention operator that replaces discrete key and value lookup with integration over a continuous, piecewise linear memory curve. Each query induces an exponential relevance density along the curve. Integrating the density and interpolated values yields exact normalized attention from closed form exponential moments, including half token boundary contributions. The gradients follow analytically from moments of order at most two, enabling parallel GPU implementations while retaining quadratic sequence complexity and the standard Transformer decoder. Compared with ordinary softmax and focal attention, CA reduces mean validation negative log likelihood by 0.0200 and 0.0480 nats per byte, respectively, winning all paired comparisons. An additional disjoint validation slice yields a 0.0457 nats per byte advantage over the strongest selected softmax baseline, with a paired 95% confidence interval. These findings motivate continuous integration as a promising attention alternative while leaving larger scale generalization open.

items.title_en: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
items.title_zh: 结合测试时训练的潜在压缩
items.abstract_en: Long contexts enlarge key--value (KV) caches, increasing memory use and attention costs during generation. Compressing these caches must preserve information for unseen questions. We introduce **Latent Compaction**, which learns a compact document-specific cache through test-time training. We initialize cache entries using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity. Training first fits attention outputs and log-normalizers to those of the full cache, with reconstruction-selected entries held fixed. It then jointly optimizes the entire cache through end-to-end distillation from the full-cache model. Model weights remain frozen throughout, and training uses only generic prompts about the document, without access to downstream questions or answers. Experiments on RULER, LongBench, and Phonebook Lookup demonstrate substantial gains over budget-matched compression baselines. On a RULER, for example, our method achieves 96.7% accuracy at 32$\times$ compression, compared with 40.0% for KVZip+. The method also transfers across model scales and families, with retrieval gains on both Qwen3 and MiniCPM5. These results show that treating the KV cache as a neural network and optimizing it with test-time training can preserve retrieval accuracy under aggressive compression. The code is released at https://www.github.com/THUNLP/latent-compaction

items.title_en: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
items.title_zh: 一个任务，多种接口：简单的跨接口一致性训练提升 LLM 智能体鲁棒性
items.abstract_en: Post-training binds the competence of an LLM agent to the interface it was trained on. Semantics-preserving perturbations of that interface, such as renaming an action or changing the notation, leave the underlying task unchanged yet make the agent worse at it. Scoring each sample independently means interface randomization only broadens this dependence from a single interface to the training interface distribution, so out-of-distribution perturbations still degrade the agent. We propose Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR), a self-supervised objective that replaces action names with uninformative identifiers and presents each training sample under two interfaces in which equivalent actions are identified by construction. CIPR penalizes the KL divergence between the action distributions induced under the two interfaces, so the policy behaves consistently across them. We evaluate CIPR in both supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training, where it improves robustness. On agentic function calling, held-out interface perturbations reduce the accuracy of a post-trained agent by nearly 25%, and CIPR recovers 10.5% while leaving accuracy on the unchanged interface intact.

items.title_en: Detection of Potato Plant Leaf Diseases using Convolutional Neural Networks
items.title_zh: 基于卷积神经网络的马铃薯植株叶片病害检测
items.abstract_en: Potato is an important food-security crop in Ethiopia, but its production is affected by foliar diseases, particularly early blight and late blight. This study develops a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify potato leaves into three categories: healthy, early blight, and late blight. The proposed model was trained using 2,215 images from the PlantVillage dataset and evaluated on an independent field dataset containing 247 images collected from potato farms in Banja, Awi Zone, Ethiopia. On PlantVillage, the model achieved 99.04% training accuracy, 98.21% validation accuracy, and 98.66% test accuracy. On the field dataset, it achieved 90.28% accuracy. The study also compares the proposed CNN with VGG16 and MobileNetV2 in terms of classification performance and computational efficiency. The proposed model contains 446,787 trainable parameters, occupies approximately 1.70 MB, and requires an average of 5.58 seconds per training epoch in the reported experimental setup, compared with 9.96 seconds for VGG16 and 7.68 seconds for MobileNetV2. The results demonstrate the potential of a compact CNN for potato leaf disease classification and highlight the importance of independent field evaluation, where image conditions are more variable than in controlled benchmark datasets. The proposed approach may support preliminary disease identification for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia and similar agricultural settings.

items.title_en: Revisiting Simple Baselines for Relational Deep Learning
items.title_zh: 重新审视关系深度学习的简单基线
items.abstract_en: Relational deep learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning end-to-end predictive models over relational databases by representing them as temporal heterogeneous graphs. Recent advances based on graph neural networks and Transformers have achieved strong performance across diverse domains. However, the effectiveness of simpler relational baselines remains underexplored, making it difficult to assess how much architectural complexity is needed to achieve strong predictive performance. Motivated by the observation that predictive signals arise from target attributes, relational attributes, and historical labels, we revisit how effectively these signals can be exploited using simple propagation methods. We adapt fixed low-pass feature propagation to relational entity graphs and train an MLP for prediction. The resulting predictions are further refined using Correct-and-Smooth, a graph-based label propagation algorithm that incorporates historical labels over task-specific meta-graphs connecting target entities. Across classification and regression tasks on RelBench, an MLP trained on neighborhood-filtered features outperforms one using only target-entity features on most tasks and recovers a substantial portion of the performance of heterogeneous GNNs. Correct-and-Smooth provides further gains from historical labels, although applying it requires a separately constructed meta-graph because connections among target entities are not directly specified by the relational entity graph. Together, our studies revisit the effectiveness of established propagation methods as simple RDL baselines while identifying canonical meta-graph construction as a key challenge for effective label propagation.

items.title_en: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
items.title_zh: 物理即网络：快速、免训练的神经仿真
items.abstract_en: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.

items.title_en: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
items.title_zh: VASPO：基于特权价值估计的自蒸馏
items.abstract_en: On-policy self-distillation provides dense supervision for reasoning models via a privileged self-teacher. However, this supervision reflects local token preferences rather than the expected return of an unguided student continuation. Recent methods combine this signal with GRPO. They use GRPO for update directions and the teacher for signal scaling. However, we demonstrate a more effective integration within PPO. Specifically, we identify complementary positional dynamics: privileged information enhances a critic's value-prediction accuracy toward the response's end, whereas self-teacher guidance is strong initially, drops mid-generation, and rebounds finally. These insights motivate Value-Augmented Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (VASPO), wherein a self-teacher and critic evaluate identical privileged information at student-generated prefixes. The critic computes token-level PPO advantages from predicted continuation returns, while the self-teacher modulates selected positive advantages via bounded probability ratios. Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VASPO improves mean accuracy over PPO by 2.59 and 1.81 percentage points on Qwen3-4B and OLMo3-7B variants, respectively, and achieves the highest mean accuracy among evaluated methods on Knights and Knaves. Our code is available at https://github.com/cii030/VASPO.

items.title_en: Bayesian Learning to Select Fair Classifiers
items.title_zh: 贝叶斯学习以选择公平分类器
items.abstract_en: Evaluations of classifiers (AI or human or agents) often assume a batch setting in which every agent produces labels on every example in a test set, which can be expensive or impractical in many contexts. This motivates online policies that adaptively select agents to query as examples arrive and update policies as outcomes are observed. We study the problem of selecting, in an online stream, the agent that best balances (i) predictive performance and (ii) subgroup fairness of a sensitive attribute, and that allows for delayed observations of true class labels. We formulate this as a Bayesian multi-armed bandit problem using Thompson Sampling, explicitly balancing accuracy and fairness. We conduct empirical evaluations on real-world datasets spanning problems involving tabular classifiers, large language models, and human labelers, demonstrating substantial reductions in regret relative to baselines. Our theoretical contributions include guarantees on the performance of the selected agent that incorporate both the accuracy and fairness aspects of the problem.

items.title_en: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
items.title_zh: 面向从纵向电子健康记录中发现的疾病轨迹的两级临床新颖性优先排序框架
items.abstract_en: Graph-based analysis of electronic health records (EHRs) yields disease-trajectory catalogs, but structural support does not establish semantic novelty. We present a two-level framework to prioritize 99,527 branching motifs previously discovered by an upstream patient-disjoint, train-only MIMIC-IV v3.1 pipeline and frozen after validation-based catalog selection. The framework separates path-level and node-to-endpoint semantic sparsity from reliability-adjusted clinical priority. Three deterministic textualizations per motif or node-target pair were embedded with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and calibrated against 166,972 pre-2023 PubMed references using mean top-20 cosine distance. Positive recombination occurred in 8.63% of motifs and had negligible effect on global ranking, whereas specificity and support/GNN reliability terms changed clinical-priority ordering. Robustness analyses across neighbor counts, templates, encoders, generic-label taxonomies, score settings, PrimeKG, and corrected density-based RND showed that broad ordering was more stable than hard top-k membership. A semantic-dose analysis did not support a monotonic relation between score and forecasting benefit after endpoint and token-count adjustment (1.96 days per SD; 95% CI, -0.75 to 4.68). In the frozen catalog-q90 high-semantic subgroup, branch-enhanced forecasting reduced conditional event-time MAE by 20.1 days (95% CI, 13.3-27.0) and sMAPE by 2.37 percentage points (95% CI, 1.81-2.93), while discrimination and endpoint-ranking differences were inconclusive. Corrected RND showed low tail agreement with the primary score (Spearman rho = 0.430; q90 Jaccard = 0.125) despite a similar aggregate timing association. These findings support representation-aware, uncertainty-aware literature-relative prioritization of discovered trajectories rather than causal discovery or clinician-adjudicated novelty.

items.title_en: Graph-Enhanced Disease Trajectory Discovery and Temporal Endpoint Forecasting from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
items.abstract_en: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can reveal disease-progression structure, while useful forecasting requires leakage-controlled discovery, censor-aware outcomes, and inspectable trajectory evidence. We developed a graph-enhanced framework in MIMIC-IV v3.1 that splits patients before graph construction, learns train-only consecutive-admission transitions, and freezes endpoint-specific branching-motif policies selected on validation data. The final catalog contained 99,527 motifs, and a time-aware Transformer retrieved at most 24 patient-compatible motifs per endpoint through endpoint-specific cross-attention. Across five training seeds, micro-AUPRC increased from 0.9330 to 0.9357, while event-time MAE decreased from 676.9 to 657.7 days (reduction 19.2 days; 95% paired patient-cluster bootstrap CI, 13.8-24.8). Timing effects were heterogeneous: MAE worsened for events within 730 days but improved by 58.9 days for events occurring after 730 days. In an exploratory internal temporal split, branch conditioning reduced conditional event-time MAE by 26.9 days (95% CI, 23.0-30.8) without evidence of better micro-AUPRC. Corrected survival evaluation over the supported 0-2,555-day interval did not establish macro C-index or integrated Brier score superiority over a matched history-only discrete-hazard model. A directed, degree-matched GNN repair substantially improved unseen-edge discovery, yet replacing GNN-derived scores within fixed motif identities did not improve downstream forecasting. These results position branching motifs as structured trajectory context whose main value is long-range timing support rather than uniformly stronger endpoint discrimination, survival prediction, or causal explanation.

items.title_en: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. We propose Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR), a single-rollout method that turns a completed trajectory's own future into token-level update weights. The generating policy snapshot scores each eligible token under its causal history and under a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback. A normalized Jensen--Shannon divergence between the two views weights the reward relative to a historical baseline, yielding bounded token credit for both successful and failed attempts, with no reference solution or learned critic. In paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared $100$-step schedule, HP-RLVR trains $1.21\times$, $1.46\times$, and $2.30\times$ faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld, using one eighth the rollouts per prompt. Accuracy is comparable overall, with HP-RLVR ahead on mathematics at all three sizes and GRPO ahead on code and ALFWorld. In ALFWorld, $43.2\%$ (4B) and $49.0\%$ (8B) of GRPO's gradient-norm records are zero, versus none for HP-RLVR.

items.title_en: Average-Reward Policy Identification from a Single Continuing Trajectory
items.abstract_en: In reinforcement learning, an agent must explore an unknown environment to learn how to make good decisions. Unlike methods that can freely sample any state--action pair, an agent learning from a single trajectory must spend additional time navigating between states. It is therefore natural to expect that learning from a single trajectory requires more experience. In this paper, we show that this additional cost is not always necessary. For average-reward reinforcement learning, we develop an algorithm that learns where to collect information while ensuring that the required samples can be obtained efficiently. We establish an upper bound on the number of interactions needed to identify a near-optimal policy. Furthermore, we prove a matching information theoretic lower bound, showing that, for a broad class of environments and at sufficiently high accuracy, learning from a single trajectory is no harder in the worst case than learning with unrestricted access to state action samples. Our results reveal that the additional complexity cost of navigation can be avoided by adapting information gathering requirements to how the environment provides information.

items.title_en: Decoupled Marginal Sharpening for Training-Free Inference-Time Scaling
items.abstract_en: We study how to improve LLM reasoning at inference time without updating model weights or using external reward models. Recent reward-free power-sampling methods define the sequence-level power target $π_α(y\mid x)\propto p_0(y\mid x)^α$, where $α>1$, which increases the relative probability of completions that are already likely under the base model. Existing methods use Metropolis--Hastings or Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to approximately sample from this target. However, two challenges arise at different levels. At the target level, full-sequence sharpening can concentrate probability on a few exact reasoning--answer trajectories, suppressing alternative paths that support the same answer. At the sampler level, finite-particle SMC can suffer from path collapse when resampling repeatedly duplicates a few high-weight prefixes. To address these challenges, we propose Decoupled Marginal Sharpening (DMS), which separately controls how strongly the model favors particular reasoning paths and how strongly it favors final answers after aggregating support across those paths. At the target level, DMS first samples from a sharpened reasoning distribution, then marginalizes the model's answer probabilities over the resulting weighted reasoning population and sharpens the induced answer marginal. Separate exponents allow mild reasoning sharpening to encourage exploration of diverse paths, followed by stronger answer-marginal sharpening to concentrate probability on answers with greater aggregate support across those paths. At the sampler level, we develop Fully Adapted Annealed SMC, which combines an annealed sequence of power targets with locally fully adapted proposals and predictive ancestor resampling. Experiments on MATH500, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval, and AIME24/25 across three base models show that DMS achieves the highest mean pass@1 among the compared methods in all tasks.

items.title_en: Lost in Translation: Why Lower Bias Scores Don't Mean Fairer Models
items.abstract_en: Bias audits of multilingual language models usually compare a model's average stereotype score in English with its average in another language and read the difference as a difference in fairness. We ask how much of that difference is noise. Auditing ten open models in eight languages, we measure how far scores move when English test items are merely reworded, test every language shift item by item, and check that the test catches shifts we inject on purpose. In all 70 model-language pairs the stereotype score falls below its English level, and for Hindi, Korean and Swahili the drop clearly exceeds what rewording English produces; most of it comes from StereoSet items. Judging every translation, we find that imperfect ones drop more, but faithful translations alone drop nearly as much. Still, a lower average does not show that a model is fairer. An item's English score predicts its translated score far less well than its reworded score (correlation 0.23, 0.27 on faithful translations, vs. 0.48), while scores stay as far from neutral, models agree on translated items, and within Hindi or Spanish a translated item's score correlates with its own rewording at 0.84 and 0.82. The average cannot distinguish lower bias from a different pattern of item-level scores. We also document three common pipeline errors that silently erase bias signal, and release our code.

items.title_en: SafeAdapt-Poker: Counterfactual Risk Calibration for Budgeted Adaptation under Opponent Shift
items.abstract_en: Opponent histories can mislead after behavioral shifts. SafeAdapt-Poker formulates budgeted adaptation under opponent shift as a dual-counterfactual sequential-control problem using only information available before each decision. At each decision the controller asks two distinct questions: what local downside a deviation from the frozen anchor would induce under matched legal continuations, and what future adaptation value would be lost by consuming part of the remaining deviation budget now. The first question is answered by a monotone strategic-risk model over deviation intensity; the second by a paired budget-state continuation model that prices current budget consumption. The controller selects among support-preserving candidate deviations by trading immediate adaptation value against these two quantities, a pathwise cumulative-KL ledger bounds total anchor-relative deviation, and a finite family of frozen controllers is screened on complete paired calibration sessions before held-out interaction. A finite-candidate perturbation bound shows that the allocation objective degrades continuously with continuation-value estimation error. Evaluation covers exact-game exploitation and safety, four opponent shifts, local-risk calibration, delayed-opportunity allocation, direct opportunity-value estimation, value-error robustness, factorial mechanism attribution, budget sensitivity, abstract-HUNL cross-play, and player/time-held-out public-history behavior. On exact Leduc the full controller attains a matched weak-pool gain of +0.0718 with a worst-opponent delta of -0.0126, raises delayed-opportunity capture from 0.6318 under myopic allocation to 0.7841 under the same session budget, and reaches +42.7 mbb/hand in abstract-HUNL cross-play; the retained public-history screen reports 0.5820 action accuracy and 0.9277 log loss versus 0.5039 and 0.9778 for a public prior.

items.title_en: Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN): An Analysis of Adaptive Action Grids in Decoupled Q-Learning
items.abstract_en: Value-based Q-learning for continuous control can discretise the action space, but the resolution of the discretisation trades early exploration against final precision. Growing Q-Networks (GQN) grow the resolution uniformly from coarse to fine. We introduce Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN), which keeps decoupled Q-learning and replaces uniform growth with an adaptive action grid: bins are added next to bins with high estimated Q-value, bins with low Q-value are pruned, and actions are chosen epsilon-greedily. On eight DeepMind Control Suite (DMControl) tasks with 2 to 12 action dimensions, SGQN has the highest mean final return among the compared methods on four, is within 1.1% of the best method on three more, and is 3.4% below Bang-Bang MPO on Walker Run, using on average 7.5 of 9 available bins per dimension. We then test whether the adaptive grid explains these results, and find that it does not. Growth activates every candidate bin and behaves like uniform growth, and removing pruning changes the return by at most 1.1%. Two other choices matter: starting from a coarse grid, since starting with all 9 bins produces collapsed seeds, and epsilon-greedy selection, since an annealed softmax lowers the return by 23% to 100%. SGQN is insensitive to its growth and pruning hyperparameters. It also differs from the GQN and DecQN baselines in other respects, notably one gradient update per environment step instead of one per eight, which we did not control for, so we do not attribute its advantage to a single component. We present SGQN as a competitive value-based method and as an analysis of which ingredients of a growing action grid matter.

items.title_en: Learning by Examples: Power Grid Steady State Analysis with a Tabular Foundation Model
items.abstract_en: Foundation models have shown strong generalization across scientific domains, but their use in power systems remains largely task-specific. We investigate whether a pretrained tabular foundation model (TFM), TabPFN, can serve as a general-purpose neural solver for power grid steady-state analysis. We evaluate the TFM on three tasks: power flow (PF) prediction, N-k contingency screening (NCS), and voltage stability margin (VSM) prediction. We performed experiments on 118- and 2000-bus systems, comparing the TFM against task-specific neural baselines. Without retraining or fine-tuning, the TFM matches or outperforms the best task-specific model in several settings across the three tasks. For 118-bus PF prediction, a variant of the TFM achieves errors of $1\times 10^{-3}$ pu for voltage magnitudes and $0.30^\circ$ for voltage angles, outperforming all baselines. On unseen N-1 contingency and close-to-infeasible PF cases, the TFM is competitive with the DCPF approximation. For millions of unseen N-2 contingencies, the TFM achieves AUCs of 0.92 and 0.95 for branch and voltage violation screening, respectively. The TFM also attains accurate VSM prediction performance for the 2000-bus system with limited labelled data. The TFM attains strong results across the tested tasks despite pretraining without any power-system-specific dataset and requiring no fine-tuning step. These results offer a glimpse into the potential of pretrained TFMs as a neural solver for a range of power grid analysis tasks.

items.title_en: What Does Disagreement Mean? A Semantic Identifiability Frontier for Pairwise Preference Learning
items.abstract_en: Pairwise comparison data are a standard supervision signal in preference learning, but disagreement in such data can reflect stable latent heterogeneity, ephemeral stochasticity, or non-binary responses hidden by a forced-choice interface. We study which of these semantic distinctions are identifiable from the feedback channel itself. We introduce a nonparametric latent semantic model with three querywise quantities: aggregate directional preference $μ_q$, persistent disagreement $τ_q$, and non-binary mass $α_q$. Under the anonymous binary channel, we prove an exact semantic fiber theorem: $μ_q$ is point-identified, whereas $(τ_q, α_q)$ vary over an explicit feasible region compatible with the same binary law. Same-annotator repeats identify $τ_q$ through a covariance identity, abstention-enabled feedback identifies $α_q$ directly, and together they point-identify the full semantic triple. We also derive finite-sample estimators, nonasymptotic concentration bounds, and semantics-aware action-recovery guarantees, and validate the theory on theorem-matched synthetic data.

items.title_en: The Accuracy Well: Nonmonotone Accuracy Dynamics at Vanishing Initialization
items.abstract_en: We study classification dynamics under small initialization and identify a pronounced non-monotone behavior of accuracy that we call the accuracy well: accuracy rises rapidly early in training, subsequently drops, and only much later recovers. We observe this phenomenon in deep linear networks, fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST, deep convolutional networks on CIFAR-10, and controlled synthetic tasks, across different losses and optimizers and in both training and test accuracy. We propose a three-stage explanation in terms of target-driven organization, a degeneracy bottleneck, and subsequent recruitment and recovery. We develop a rigorous theory of these dynamics for shallow and deep linear networks, showing in particular that high accuracy can emerge while the predictor and the change in loss remain asymptotically vanishing, before continued optimization causes accuracy to deteriorate. For a simple synthetic classification task, we prove an extreme instance in which accuracy asymptotically rises to 100%, collapses to 0, and later recovers permanently to 100%. Our results show that classification accuracy can reveal aspects of learning dynamics that are not captured by the training loss alone.

items.title_en: Continual Learning for Reliable In-Sequence Molecular Communication
items.abstract_en: This paper considers reliable in-sequence molecular communication, where bio-nanomachines exchange molecule-encoded information in a specified order, and investigates a new simulation-based method to incrementally evaluate communication protocols by gradually increasing the complexity of experimental settings. The proposed method, called Affine Memory Replay (AMR), builds a continual learning (CL) model to estimate communication performance between bio-nanomachines. AMR stores past simulation samples and synthesizes additional replay samples through interpolation and extrapolation between past samples. Through incremental performance estimation tasks, it replays both past and synthetic samples to regularize model updates, helping the model adapt to new experimental settings while retaining knowledge from earlier ones. Experimental results show that AMR significantly outperforms existing CL methods in maintaining overall estimation accuracy across sequentially learned estimation tasks. It effectively balances memory stability and learning plasticity under moderate training cost.

items.title_en: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning
items.abstract_en: Tabular foundation models enable in-context learning by predicting unseen observations from a labeled support table without task-specific parameter updates. Despite recent advances, most existing approaches rely on dense architectures that apply the same transformations across features and datasets. We introduce OrionMoE-Small, a compact tabular foundation model that combines distribution-aware representations with dataset-conditioned sparse mixture-of-experts computation. Built on a dual-axis Transformer architecture, OrionMoE-Small selectively activates experts along the feature axis, with routing decisions informed by both individual feature representations and the broader dataset context. This design enables adaptive allocation of computation across heterogeneous tabular problems while retaining a shared computational pathway across tasks. OrionMoE-Small is pretrained entirely on synthetic classification tasks generated from a structured causal prior and performs downstream prediction without gradient-based adaptation. Experiments across multiple tabular benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance against substantially larger foundation models, with particularly strong results on small-context and high-dimensional datasets. Further analysis reveals favorable relative performance under class imbalance and highlights the importance of feature composition.

items.title_en: Tracking a Small Set of Experts in Online Convex Optimization
items.abstract_en: For the fundamental problem of prediction from expert advice, Freund asked whether one could compete with a comparator that switches $k$ times among only $m$ experts. For a discrete set of experts, this problem was resolved by Bousquet and Warmuth (2020), who gave an efficient algorithm with optimal regret matching the information-theoretic limit. We study the analogous problem in online convex optimization, where the action space is continuous. An inefficient algorithm can be derived by discretizing the action space and applying the Bousquet--Warmuth algorithm, giving regret of $\widetilde{O}(md+k)$, while the best known efficient algorithm for this problem has regret $\widetilde{O}(dk)$. We show that this computational inefficiency is inherent, establishing a separation between the information-theoretic and polynomial-time regret achievable for this problem. Specifically, under the hypergraphic planted-clique conjecture, we show that for every polynomial-time algorithm there exist instances for which it incurs at least $(k\sqrt d)^{1-o(1)}$ regret.

items.title_en: One Size Does Not Fit All: Curvature-Aware Adaptive Perturbation for SAM
items.abstract_en: Poor generalisation in deep neural networks is frequently associated with convergence to sharp minima. Sharpness-Aware Minimisation (SAM) improves generalisation of deep neural networks by minimising a combination of the training loss and the local sharpness of the loss landscape, biasing convergence towards flat minima. However, SAM relies on a fixed perturbation radius $ρ$ that ignores local curvature, leading to inefficient behaviour: the perturbation may be too small to escape poor basins defined by sharp local minima, or too large to allow convergence to solutions with good loss-sharpness tradeoff. We reinterpret $ρ$ as the intensity of the perturbation signal and propose Curvature-Aware Adaptive Perturbation for SAM (CAP-SAM), a geometry-aware method that modulates the perturbation radius based on a sharpness ratio, enabling a more effective search for robust minima on the loss landscape. We prove that CAP-SAM preserves the same convergence rate as standard SAM in non-convex stochastic settings. Extensive experiments indicate that our approach consistently outperforms SAM and its most prominent variants across diverse network architectures on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet.

items.title_en: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
items.abstract_en: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.

items.title_en: Hyperspherical Contrastive Representations Unlock Planning and Exploration
items.abstract_en: We develop a self-supervised reinforcement learning algorithm that learns to build towers of up to eight cubes from scratch, without prior data, rewards, demonstrations, or pretrained models. Our method, Contrastive Planning via Spherical Linear Interpolation (C-Slerp), uses contrastive representations as reusable building blocks and repeatedly composes them to infer a sequence of intermediate waypoints. Under our hyperspherical parameterization, the learned representations allow intermediate waypoints to be inferred in closed form through spherical linear interpolation, without training a separate high-level policy or performing graph search. Importantly, the representation geometry also tells us how to adjust the number of waypoints based on the difficulty of each goal-reaching problem. Experiments show that our method succeeds on long-horizon navigation and robotic manipulation tasks, including settings where strong baselines fail to achieve a single success. Ablations further show that using a fixed number of waypoints substantially degrades performance, highlighting the importance of adapting the plan to task difficulty.

items.title_en: Posterior Frequencies and the Cost of Not Fitting: A Correction to a Memorization Lower Bound
items.abstract_en: Feldman's memorization lower bound assigns a frequency coefficient based on how often a point appears in the training sample. We give an exact three-point counterexample to its conditional and averaged forms, using independent fair labels and a permutation-equivariant learner. A sequence of sampling priors makes the ratio of the proposed penalty to actual excess risk grow exponentially, ruling out a universal positive constant-factor repair. The priors vary with sample size, the offending profiles become rare, and both quantities vanish. Retaining the original model, we obtain an exact replacement using full-sample posterior probabilities. Under exchangeability, these depend on multiplicity and the complete frequency profile. We characterize the largest multiplicity-only coefficients valid for unrestricted learners. The original coefficient has the posterior-mean form of Good's exact frequency formula and is an occupancy-weighted average of the corrected coefficients.

items.title_en: Training Language Models to Fail Gracefully
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning makes language models better at solving tasks, but the same mechanism also rewards guessing. When success is the only way to earn reward, opting for a safe fallback is always worse than a long-shot attempt. When a wrong action can corrupt a database or ship broken code, that incentive can be costly. Therefore, we propose training models to fail gracefully: to preserve successful behavior whenever possible while learning to execute a safe fallback policy when acting would be unreliable. However, naively using policy gradients with intermediate reward for fallback behavior is brittle due to unfavorable optimization dynamics. We address this challenge with GracefulRL, which reshapes the optimization landscape to promote graceful failure. Importantly, this behavior emerges directly from outcome-level reward signals, without annotations specifying when to fall back or additional inference-time machinery such as a verifier. Across a range of tasks and scales, we train models that largely preserve their task-solving capability while selectively falling back when acting would be unreliable. More broadly, our results show that reinforcement learning can not only incentivize models to succeed, but also to reason about the limits of their capabilities and change course when they determine that success is out of reach.

items.title_en: HRTF Upsampling and Personalization via Neural Operators
items.abstract_en: Head-related transfer function (HRTF) spatial upsampling from sparse measurements is a fundamental challenge in personalized binaural audio. We formulate HRTF upsampling as an operator learning problem and introduce SPARO, a neural operator that maps sparse measurements at a set of spatial directions to the HRTF field, a continuous representation that can be queried at arbitrary positions. SPARO projects the measurements onto a learned set of spherical latent modes, processes the latent modes with Transformer blocks, and decodes the resulting representations at query directions. On SONICOM, using the LAP24 measurement configuration, SPARO attains the best log-spectral distortion (LSD) and interaural level difference (ILD) error at every sparsity level from 3 to 100 measurements (18% lower LSD and 43% lower ILD error than the strongest baseline at 100 measurements) while remaining competitive in interaural time difference (ITD) error. It reconstructs a dense HRTF 15 to 373 times faster than the leading neural-field method RANF. We further validate the approach on HUTUBS, demonstrating its effectiveness across HRTF datasets.

items.title_en: From Human Corrections to Learned Segmentations: A Critical Mathematical Review of Information, Learning, and Human Effort
items.abstract_en: When does a human correction become useful learning, and what establishes better segmentation at matched human effort? This critical narrative review follows feedback through its selection, learner update, and evaluation. It compares active learning, machine teaching, interactive segmentation, and sequential predictive evaluation using a common mathematical account of target information, predictive error, response predictability, and human work. An exact Bayesian update converts evaluation-label information into expected log-loss improvement; an excess-risk decomposition explains what an approximate learner can lose. Conditional information decompositions separate the roles of selected locations, labels, and displayed context. Empirical comparisons show why response protocols, update mechanisms, and effort denominators matter, distinguishing current-mask refinement from reusable learning and simulated interaction from human evidence. We identify what logs can reveal, what requires independent evaluation, and what remains model-dependent. The resulting research priorities are to test what selection reveals, whether using it improves assimilation, and whether the resulting interaction policy benefits segmentation at matched effort. These are distinct claims: predicting a teacher's responses need not identify human intentions or establish better learning. No new acquisition algorithm or empirical superiority is claimed.

items.title_en: FOLD: Position-Free Far Memory with Local Order for Long-Context Speculative Decoding
items.abstract_en: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM generation through lightweight drafting and parallel verification. It is particularly promising for long inputs, where KV-cache access costs can be amortized over multiple accepted tokens. Yet most drafters are trained on short sequences and degrade on long inputs, while long-context training is costly. Existing training-free approaches restrict the context window, rescale positions, or augment recent context with retrieved distant entries. Drafters, however, read target hidden states that already encode contextual and positional information, and their lightweight architecture makes full-history attention affordable. We propose FOLD, a training-free method that preserves exact local positions and treats all distant entries as far memory at a shared position. To counter attention dilution as the memory grows, we sharpen attention within it to emphasize relevant entries while separately controlling its total weight relative to the local window. Across six target-drafter pairs and diverse benchmarks of up to 256K tokens, FOLD predominantly delivers the highest speedup, with the best case more than doubling the speedup over autoregressive decoding, from 2.08$\times$ to 4.22$\times$.

items.title_en: To Stack or Not to Stack? Jacobian Conditioning and the Benefits of Depth in Metasurface-Based Linear Transformation Synthesis
items.title_zh: 堆叠还是不堆叠？基于超表面的线性变换合成中的 Jacobian 条件数与深度带来的收益
items.abstract_en: This paper investigates when and why stacking programmable metasurfaces into Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIMs) improves linear transformation synthesis at a fixed phase-control budget. The analysis shows that algebraic Jacobian rank alone is insufficient to characterize practical synthesis, which also depends on the strength and balance of the sensitivity directions generated by the available controls. A layer-resolved analysis of the cascade model explains how inter-layer propagation can generate complementary sensitivity directions. The relevance of this mechanism is then assessed using an S-parameter multiport model that includes electromagnetic coupling and multiple scattering. Numerical results in near- and far-field sensing scenarios show that distributing the same control resources across multiple layers can strengthen weak transformation directions, improve Jacobian conditioning, and substantially enhance synthesis accuracy. These findings explain why increasing depth can offer benefits that are not obtained by simply enlarging a single programmable surface, and identify layer complementarity and Jacobian conditioning as useful criteria for SIM architecture design.
items.abstract_zh: 本文研究在相位控制预算固定时，将可编程超表面堆叠为堆叠智能超表面（SIM）为何以及在何时能改进线性变换合成。分析表明，仅凭代数上的 Jacobian 秩不足以刻画实际合成效果，它还取决于现有控制量所产生的敏感度方向的强度与均衡程度。对级联模型的逐层分析解释了层间传播如何产生互补的敏感度方向。随后用一个包含电磁耦合与多次散射的 S 参数多端口模型评估该机制的相关性。近场与远场感知场景的数值结果表明，把相同的控制资源分配到多个层，可以增强薄弱的变换方向、改善 Jacobian 条件数，并显著提升合成精度。这些发现解释了为何增加深度能带来单纯扩大单个可编程表面所无法获得的收益，并指出层互补性与 Jacobian 条件数是 SIM 架构设计的有用准则。
items.highlight_zh: 分层比单面大更好：看 Jacobian 条件数
items.digest_zh: 1) 研究了什么问题：把可编程超表面一层层叠起来（Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces, SIM），在相位控制资源总量不变的前提下，究竟能不能、以及在什么条件下能更准确地合成想要的线性变换？2) 用了什么方法：先用级联模型做逐层理论分析，指出光看 Jacobian 的秩不够，还要看各个控制量能产生的敏感度方向有多强、是否均衡；层间传播可以生成互相补充的敏感方向。再用包含电磁耦合与多次散射的 S 参数多端口模型检验这一机制是否在真实电磁条件下依然成立。3) 有什么结果：在近场与远场感知场景中，把同样的控制资源分摊到多层，能够增强原本薄弱的变换方向、改善 Jacobian 条件数，合成精度大幅提升。4) 为何重要：它给出了「深度优于单纯把单面做大」的机理解释，并把层互补性和 Jacobian 条件数立为 SIM 架构设计的实用判据。

items.title_en: Hypothesis Selection via Weighted Medians
items.abstract_en: Given $n$ distributions (hypotheses) $\mathcal H=\{H_1,\ldots,H_n\}$ and samples from an unknown target distribution $P$, proper hypothesis selection seeks a distribution whose total variation distance to $P$ is close to the best achievable within the known distributions. We give an algorithm that, using $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$ target samples, running in $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$ time, with probability at least $1-δ$, returns $H_{\hat i}$ satisfying $d_\mathrm{TV}(P,H_{\hat i})\leq 3\min_{i\in[n]}d_\mathrm{TV}(P,H_i)+\varepsilon.$ The algorithm achieves the optimal approximation factor and sample complexity. The running time improves the dependence on the failure probability from polynomial to logarithmic in the state-of-the-art bound $\tilde{O}(n\varepsilon^{-2}δ^{-1})$ of Aamand, Aliakbarpour, Chen, and Silwal (COLT 2026), thereby answering their Question~2.

items.title_en: ReAl: Refine neural operators via aligning dynamical flow
items.abstract_en: Neural partial differential equation (PDE) surrogates trained with mean squared error (MSE) can capture dominant dynamics but often lose high-frequency information and fine-scale structures. Generative models (e.g., Flow Matching) can capture the distribution of fine-scale details, yet stochastic errors may accumulate during autoregressive rollouts and compromise long-term stability. To address these limitations, we introduce Refine and Align(ReAl), a model-agnostic plug-in that augments pretrained PDE surrogates to improve the reconstruction of high-frequency structures associated with complex physical phenomena. In the refinement stage, a conditional flow-matching model learns the residual distribution around the deterministic base prediction, recovering missing fine-scale structures while retaining the dominant dynamics. In the alignment stage, to mitigate the generative discrepancies amplified in the autoregressive rollout, particularly in chaotic systems, we generate multiple trajectories from the same input and reinforce the refiner with trajectory-level rewards, thereby achieving long-horizon dynamical alignment. Experiments across diverse surrogate architectures and PDE tasks demonstrate that ReAl consistently improves high-frequency fidelity, forecasting accuracy, and long-horizon stability.

items.title_en: Fractional is Better: Learnable Derivative Orders in Neural Operator Learning
items.abstract_en: Neural operators learn mappings between function spaces, enabling fast surrogate solutions to partial differential equations. Despite remarkable architectural diversity, these methods often share a common input representation: raw coordinate-value pairs $(x, u(x))$. We ask whether inputs aligned with PDE differential structure can improve learning. Through Picard iteration on mild solutions, we show that derivatives of the input appear explicitly in the solution operator, suggesting that providing derivative features should reduce the network's implicit differentiation burden. We prove this intuition: providing derivative features improves approximation bounds from $O(W^{-(s-m)/d})$ to $O(W^{-s/d})$, where $W$ is parameter count, $s$ is input regularity, $m$ is the PDE order, and $d$ is spatial dimension. Our central finding, however, is a surprise: the optimal derivative order $β^*$ is strictly less than the PDE order $m$. This gap arises from a bias-variance tradeoff in spectral space that we characterize in closed form. Learning $β$ from data achieves automatic spectral regularization. We introduce $\partial$-NO (del-NO), for derivative-augmented neural operators, an architecture-agnostic augmentation that provides learnable fractional derivative features to any neural operator backbone. Across benchmark problems and architectures, $\partial$-NO consistently improves prediction accuracy, with learned orders that reflect a representation of known physics modulated by noise and finite-sample constraints.

items.title_en: Closed-Form Optimal Weight Splitting for Matrix-Vector Multiply on Noisy In-Memory Accelerators
items.title_zh: 噪声存内计算加速器上矩阵-向量乘法的闭式最优权重拆分
items.abstract_en: Analog in-memory computing performs the matrix-vector multiplications of neural networks directly inside the memory array, which saves time and energy. But each memory cell stores only a few levels and is noisy, so one cell cannot hold a weight precisely. The standard fix is to split each weight across several cells, like digits of a number. The base of this split decides the trade-off: a large base gives fine resolution but amplifies the noise, and a base near one averages the noise but wastes resolution. The best-known prior analysis considers only the noise, and so it always picks a base of one. We propose a principled method that also accounts for the limited number of levels per cell. It gives the optimal base in closed form, from a single measurement of the device noise. On a device-physics simulator, the optimal split is 3.3 dB more accurate than the common base-16 split, and it beats equal splitting in end-application accuracy.
items.abstract_zh: 模拟存内计算直接在存储阵列内部完成神经网络的矩阵-向量乘法，从而节省时间与能耗。但每个存储单元只能存储少数几个电平且带有噪声，单个单元无法精确承载一个权重。标准做法是把每个权重拆分到多个单元，如同一个数的各位数字。拆分的基数决定权衡：基数大则分辨率高但会放大噪声，基数接近一虽能平均噪声却浪费分辨率。此前最知名的分析只考虑噪声，因此总是选择基数为 1。我们提出一种有原则的方法，同时考虑每个单元有限电平数的限制，仅凭一次器件噪声测量即可闭式给出最优基数。在器件物理模拟器上，最优拆分的精度比常用的 base-16 拆分高 3.3 dB，并在端到端应用精度上优于均等拆分。
items.highlight_zh: 闭式最优拆分基数，比 base-16 精确 3.3 dB
items.digest_zh: 1) 研究了什么问题：模拟存内计算把权重直接存进存储阵列，省时省能，但单元只有少数几个电平又有噪声，单个单元存不准一个权重，于是把权重拆成几段存到多个单元里，像写一个数的各位数字。关键参数是「基数」：基数大分辨率细但噪声被放大，基数接近 1 能靠平均压噪但浪费分辨率。2) 用了什么方法：以往最好的分析只考虑噪声，所以总选基数 1；本文同时把每单元电平数有限这一约束纳入建模，从一次器件噪声测量出发，推导出最优基数的闭式解。3) 有什么结果：在器件物理模拟器上，最优拆分的精度比业界常用的 base-16 拆分高 3.3 dB，并且在下游应用精度上超过简单的均等拆分。4) 为何重要：它给出了一个即插即用、有理论依据的拆分参数选择规则，兼顾噪声与量化，直接提升模拟存内加速器的有效精度。

items.title_en: Beyond Expert Rankings: Contrast Calibration for Mixed-Precision MoE Quantization
items.abstract_en: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models activate only a few experts per token, yet all expert weights must be stored. Mixed-precision quantization reduces this storage cost by assigning higher bit-widths to sensitive experts and lower bit-widths to resilient ones, but expert rankings alone do not determine how strongly to weight their errors. To address this gap, we propose NatScale, a contrast-calibrated allocation framework for mixed-precision MoE quantization. It uses a model-specific power transformation to calibrate gradient-based expert weights to an information-theoretic contrast target while preserving rankings. We jointly evaluate each expert's gate, up and down configurations to estimate its output error. We then combine these errors and calibrated weights with an existing prior based on weight spectra, variance and precision decay to select configurations under a storage budget. Across three models, NatScale achieves the lowest native-to-quantized KL divergence and the highest top-token agreement in all nine settings against five allocation baselines. It also yields the lowest perplexity in seven settings. These findings highlight the importance of objective-aware precision allocation.

items.title_en: Lifted State Policy Optimization: Internalizing Self-Correction through Transition Geometry
items.abstract_en: Preference optimization ranks final answers and trajectory RL maximizes aggregate returns, yet neither credits the local change that turns a flawed reasoning state into a better one. We introduce Lifted State Policy Optimization (LSPO), which establishes this finite, cost-adjusted transition as the primary unit of learning. Each textual answer is augmented with a learned continuous coordinate, forming a lifted state that an energy function evaluates and orders. A shaped reward drives energy descent net of edit and step costs, and an internalization loss absorbs selected low-energy answers into the direct generator. On Qwen3.5-27B, the resulting single-pass policy reaches 71.8% aggregate accuracy across mathematics, science, code, and logic benchmarks, matching test-time reflection at 71.9% with 28% lower latency and 25.8% fewer tokens. The pattern holds across dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, and matched controls confirm that transition credit and the lifted coordinate each contribute, as does answer internalization. Our code is available at https://github.com/Venomrko/lspo.

items.title_en: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection
items.title_zh: NeuroDETR：面向异步脑电事件检测的多尺度离散时空令牌化
items.abstract_en: Asynchronous EEG event detection supports practical brain-computer interfaces by identifying event classes and temporal boundaries directly from continuous recordings without predefined event boundaries at inference time. The primary challenge lies in extracting event-related patterns embedded in ongoing background activity. To address this, we propose \textbf{NeuroDETR}, a discrete spatiotemporal multiscale framework that combines structured tokenization with event-aware feature refinement. Multiscale temporal codebooks capture brief responses and sustained dynamics, while Spatial-Pyramid VQ hierarchically encodes spatial structure across EEG channels. These complementary representations form a compact event memory for jointly classifying events and estimating their onsets and offsets.
